V2G20-2096.text: [V2G20-2096] In case authorization has already been completed by the time AuthorizationSetupReq is received by the SECC or authorization is not necessary, the SECC shall only offer EIM in AuthorizationSetupRes.

atoms.notes: Checks if authorization has already been completed or is not necessary.
The SECC shall only offer EIM in the AuthorizationSetupRes message.
Ensures OfferedAuthorizationModes is of type ENUMERATED.
Ensures OfferedAuthorizationModes is a mandatory field.
Specifies that the next message after receiving AuthorizationSetupReq should be AuthorizationSetupRes.

V2G20-2097.text: NOTE 7 In this case the EVCC will follow [V2G20-2097], [V2G20-2098] or [V2G20-5046], depending on the energy transfer mode selected.

atoms.expr: IF EnergyTransferModeSelected THEN FOLLOW [V2G20-2097] OR [V2G20-2098] OR [V2G20-5046]
atoms.notes: This atom describes the branching logic based on the selected energy transfer mode.

V2G20-2098.text: NOTE 7 In this case the EVCC will follow [V2G20-2097], [V2G20-2098] or [V2G20-5046], depending on the energy transfer mode selected.

atoms.expr: if (EnergyTransferModeSelected == 'DC') then follow [V2G20-2097]; if (EnergyTransferModeSelected == 'AC') then follow [V2G20-2098]; if (EnergyTransferModeSelected == 'Wireless') then follow [V2G20-5046]
atoms.notes: This sequence constraint dictates which requirement to follow based on the selected energy transfer mode.
This guard ensures that the EVCC has received a ServiceDiscoveryReq before sending SVCDiscoveryRes.
The EVCC shall send a SVCDiscoveryRes message.
The ResponseCode field in SVCDiscoveryRes must be set to 'OK'.
The ServiceID field in SVCDiscoveryRes is mandatory.
The EVCC must send SVCDiscoveryRes within the specified timeout.
After receiving a ServiceDiscoveryReq, the next allowed response is SVCDiscoveryRes.
If the ResponseCode is not 'OK', an error handling mechanism should be triggered.

V2G20-2100.text: [V2G20-2100] During a standby period with conductive charging and ACD, the physical connection shall be maintained throughout the entire service session.

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the physical connection is maintained during the entire service session when in a standby period with conductive charging and ACD.

atoms.expr: ChargingSessionState == STANDBY && ChargingMode == CONDUCTIVE && ACD == TRUE
atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the requirement applies only during a standby period with conductive charging and ACD.

V2G20-2101.text: [V2G20-2101] If [V2G20-710] applies, the EVCC may stop the V2G communication session when V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timer is equal or larger than V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timeout and no parameter EVSE_Processing_equal to "Finished" has been received.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the ongoing timer exceeds the timeout.
This guard ensures that no 'Finished' processing status has been received from the SECC.
This guard references another requirement, indicating a dependency on its conditions being met.
This action specifies that the EVCC may terminate the V2G communication session under the given conditions.

V2G20-2102.text: [V2G20-2102] If [V2G20-712] applies, the SECC may send ResponseCode equal to "FAILED" when V2G_SECC_Ongoing_Timer is equal or larger than V2G_SECC_Ongoing_Performance_Time and no parameter EVSEProcessing equal to "Finished" has been sent.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the conditions specified in [V2G20-712] apply, the ongoing timer exceeds the performance time, and no 'Finished' processing status has been sent.
The SECC sends a ResponseCode of 'FAILED' under the specified conditions.

V2G20-2103.text: [V2G20-2103] Unless defined otherwise DepartureTime in all messages shall always be larger than zero.

atoms.notes: This invariant applies to all messages where DepartureTime is present, ensuring it is always greater than zero unless explicitly defined otherwise.

V2G20-2104.text: [V2G20-2104] Unless defined otherwise DepartureTime in all messages shall express the offset in seconds from the point in time of sending this message, which is marked in the TimeStamp element of the common V2G message header.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the DepartureTime field correctly represents the offset in seconds from the TimeStamp.
This guard checks if there is no other definition for DepartureTime, ensuring the default behavior applies.

atoms.expr: forall m in messages: if m.DepartureTime exists then m.DepartureTime = m.TimeStamp + DepartureTimeOffset
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that throughout the session, whenever DepartureTime is present, it adheres to the specified calculation.

V2G20-2105.text: [V2G20-2105] If EVSENotification is set to MeteringConfirmation in the ChargeLoopRes, the SECC shall provide a NotificationMaxDelay value.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVSENotification field in the ChargeLoopRes message is set to 'MeteringConfirmation'.
This action specifies that the SECC must provide a value for the NotificationMaxDelay field when the guard condition is met.
This field constraint ensures that the NotificationMaxDelay field becomes mandatory when EVSENotification is 'MeteringConfirmation'.

V2G20-2106.text: [V2G20-2106] When receiving the SessionSetupReq with the parameter SessionID equal to zero, the SECC shall generate a new (not stored) SessionID value different from zero and return this value in the SessionSetupRes message header.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the received SessionSetupReq has a SessionID equal to zero.
The SECC generates a new SessionID value that is not stored and different from zero.
Ensures the generated SessionID is different from zero in the SessionSetupRes message header.

atoms.expr: SessionID is unique and not stored
atoms.notes: Ensures the generated SessionID is unique and not previously stored during the session.

V2G20-2107.text: [V2G20-2107] The EVCC shall send one (1) contract certificate chain in the element ContractCertificateChain.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the EVCC sends exactly one contract certificate chain in the specified message.
This atom specifies that the ContractCertificateChain field is mandatory in the CertificateInstallationRes message.

V2G20-2108.text: [V2G20-2108] GenChallenge shall be generated per random number generation requirements as defined by 7.3.7.

atoms.notes: The GenChallenge is generated according to the random number generation requirements specified in section 7.3.7.
The type of GenChallenge must be RandomNumber as per the requirements in section 7.3.7.
The GenChallenge field is mandatory in the SAP_Req message.
The domain of GenChallenge must adhere to the specifications provided in section 7.3.7.

V2G20-2113.text: [V2G20-2113] After receiving the PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode equal to "OK" as a response to a previous PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress equal to "Standby", the EVCC shall send a ChargeLoopReq while V2G_EVCC_Sequence_Timer is smaller than V2G_EVCC_Sequence_Performance_Time.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures the correct conditions after receiving PowerDeliveryRes.
The EVCC sends a ChargeLoopReq under the specified conditions.

V2G20-2115.text: [V2G20-2115] At the point in time when requesting pause by setting the parameter EVSENotification to "Pause" in dynamic control mode, the SECC shall ensure that the applied power level is equal to 0 kW (no current drawn by EV or EVSE).

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the SECC is in the process of requesting a pause.
This invariant ensures that the applied power level is zero when a pause is requested.

atoms.expr: EVSENotification.type == 'Enum' AND EVSENotification.mandatory == true AND EVSENotification.domain == ['Pause', 'Resume']
atoms.notes: This field constraint specifies the type, mandatory status, and domain of the EVSENotification field.
This assumption ensures that neither the EV nor the EVSE is drawing any current during the pause state.

V2G20-2116.text: [V2G20-2116] At the point in time when requesting standby by PowerDeliveryReq with parameter ChargeProgress="Standby", the EVCC shall ensure that the applied power level is equal to zero kW (no current drawn by EV or EVSE).

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the ChargeProgress parameter is set to 'Standby' when the PowerDeliveryReq message is sent.
The EVCC must ensure that the applied power level is set to zero kW when sending the PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress='Standby'.
While in the state where ChargeProgress is 'Standby', the applied power level must remain at zero kW.

atoms.expr: No current drawn by EV or EVSE
atoms.notes: It is assumed that neither the EV nor the EVSE draws any current when the applied power level is zero kW.

V2G20-2117.text: [V2G20-2117] After receiving a PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode equal to "OK" as a response to the previous PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress equal to "Standby", the EVCC shall not process any elements in the ChargeLoopRes except EVSEStatus, ResponseCode, MeterInfo and Receipt, until the next PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress set to "Start", "Stop", or "Renegotiate" is send.

atoms.notes: The EVCC should ignore all elements in ChargeLoopRes except the specified ones.
The next PowerDeliveryReq must have ChargeProgress set to 'Start', 'Stop', or 'Renegotiate'.

V2G20-2118.text: [V2G20-2118] After sending a PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode equal to "OK" as a response to the previous PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress equal to "Standby", the SECC shall not process any elements in the ChargeLoopReq except MeterInfoRequested and DisplayParameters, until the next PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress set to "Start", "Stop", or "Renegotiate" is received.

atoms.notes: Checks if the previous message was a PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode OK and ChargeProgress Standby.
Ensures that only MeterInfoRequested and DisplayParameters are processed in ChargeLoopReq.
Waits for the next PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Start, Stop, or Renegotiate.
Ensures that only MeterInfoRequested and DisplayParameters are processed until the next relevant PowerDeliveryReq is received.

V2G20-2119.text: [V2G20-2119] After receiving a PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode equal to "OK" as a response to the previous PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress equal to "Standby", and if EVCC selected the service parameter MobilityNeedsMode set to 2, the EVCC shall process the elements TargetSOC, MinimumSOC, DepartureTime and AckMaxDelay in the DC_ChargeLoopRes messages.

atoms.notes: Verifies that the MobilityNeedsMode is set to 2 by the EVCC.
The EVCC processes specific fields from the DC_ChargeLoopRes message.
Ensures that the processing happens after receiving the correct PowerDeliveryRes and before sending/receiving DC_ChargeLoopRes.

V2G20-2120.text: [V2G20-2120] After receiving a PowerDeliveryRes with ResponseCode equal to "OK" as a response to the previous PowerDeliveryReq message with ChargeProgress equal to "Standby", and if EVCC selected the service parameter MobilityNeedsMode set to 2, the EVCC shall process the elements TargetSOC, MinimumSOC, DepartureTime and AckMaxDelay in the AC_ChargeLoopRes messages.

atoms.notes: Verifies that the MobilityNeedsMode is set to 2 by the EVCC.
The EVCC processes specific fields from the AC_ChargeLoopRes message.
Ensures TargetSOC is an integer and mandatory in AC_ChargeLoopRes.
Ensures MinimumSOC is an integer and mandatory in AC_ChargeLoopRes.
Ensures DepartureTime is an integer and mandatory in AC_ChargeLoopRes.
Ensures AckMaxDelay is an integer and mandatory in AC_ChargeLoopRes.

V2G20-2121.text: [V2G20-2121] If no power is available at the EVSE, the SECC shall set GoToPause to TRUE and set the first PowerScheduleEntry to 0W.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if no power is available at the EVSE.
The SECC sets GoToPause to TRUE when no power is available.
The SECC sets the first PowerScheduleEntry to 0W when no power is available.

V2G20-2122.text: [V2G20-2122] If DC was selected as the energy transfer mode, the first PowerScheduleEntry in the ScheduleExchangeRes is set to 0W and GoToPause is set to TRUE, the EVCC shall skip DC_CableCheck and DC_PreCharge and directly send a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Pause.

atoms.notes: Checks if DC mode is selected and the first PowerScheduleEntry is set to 0W with GoToPause set to TRUE.
The EVCC skips the DC_CableCheck and DC_PreCharge steps.
The EVCC sends a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Pause.
Ensures that after skipping DC_CableCheck and DC_PreCharge, the next allowed request is PowerDeliveryReq.

V2G20-2123.text: [V2G20-2123] If the EVCC wants to start with a pause, after having received ScheduleExchangeRes, the EVCC shall send a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Stop.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC wants to start with a pause and has already received the ScheduleExchangeRes.
This action specifies that the EVCC shall send a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Stop.
This field constraint ensures that the ChargeProgress field in PowerDeliveryReq is set to Stop.
This sequence constraint ensures that the next message sent by the EVCC after receiving ScheduleExchangeRes is PowerDeliveryReq.

V2G20-2124.text: [V2G20-2124] If EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest and EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest are sent by the EVCC, they always need to be sent together.

applies_to_messages: all messages containing EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest or EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that if EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest is present in a message, then EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest must also be present.

applies_to_messages: all messages containing EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest or EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that if EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest is present in a message, then EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest must also be present.

V2G20-2125.text: [V2G20-2125] If the EVCC provides EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest and EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest, they shall follow the following mathematical relationship:

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the maximum energy request is not less than the minimum energy request.
The EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest field is optional according to the specification.
The EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest field is optional according to the specification.

atoms.expr: if EVMaximumV2XEnergyRequest is present then EVMinimumV2XEnergyRequest must also be present
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that if the maximum energy request is provided, the minimum energy request must also be provided.

V2G20-2126.text: [V2G20-2126] The maximum length of EMAID shall be 255 characters.

atoms.notes: This constraint applies to the EMAID field globally across all messages where it may appear.

V2G20-2127.text: [V2G20-2127] SECCID shall be an alphanumeric string with a length of minimum 39 and maximum 255 characters (i.e.

atoms.notes: This constraint applies to the SECCID field globally, ensuring it meets the specified length and character requirements.

V2G20-2128.text: [V2G20-2128] Characters restricted for usage in WMI by ISO 3780 shall not be used in SECCID.

atoms.expr: SECCID does not contain characters restricted by ISO 3780
atoms.notes: This constraint ensures compliance with ISO 3780 character restrictions for the SECCID field.

V2G20-2129.text: [V2G20-2129] If in the supportedAppProtocolReq, an energy transfer mode is offered based on ISO 15118-20, all features implemented for this energy transfer mode in older generations of the document still need to be supported for ISO 15118-20.

atoms.notes: Checks if the energy transfer mode offered is based on ISO 15118-20.
Ensures that all features implemented for the energy transfer mode in older generations are supported.

atoms.expr: forall m in messages where m.EnergyTransferMode == ISO_15118_20 -> m.SupportedFeatures includes older_generation_features
atoms.notes: Ensures that throughout the session, any message with ISO 15118-20 energy transfer mode supports older generation features.

V2G20-2130.text: [V2G20-2130] If the SA provided a PriceSchedule along with a signature, the SECC shall include the PriceSchedule along with the signature in the ScheduleExchangeRes.

atoms.notes: Checks if both PriceSchedule and its signature were provided by the SA.
The SECC includes the PriceSchedule and its signature in the ScheduleExchangeRes message.
Ensures that both PriceSchedule and Signature fields are mandatory in the ScheduleExchangeRes message.

V2G20-2132.text: [V2G20-2132] If an EVCC supports the service DC and intends to offer it for this V2G communication session, it shall add an AppProtocol element to the supportedAppProtocolReq with ProtocolNamespace set to "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:DC", VersionNumberMajor set to "1" and VersionNumberMinor set to "0".

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC supports and intends to offer the DC service.
This action specifies adding an AppProtocol element with specific values to the SupportedAppProtocolReq message.
This field constraint ensures the correct values are set for the ProtocolNamespace, VersionNumberMajor, and VersionNumberMinor fields within the AppProtocol element.

V2G20-2133.text: [V2G20-2133] The namespaces "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:CommonMessages" and "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:CommonTypes" shall never be used in the context of the supportedAppProtocolReq.

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the specified namespaces are never used within the SupportedAppProtocolReq message.

V2G20-2134.text: [V2G20-2134] Whenever a TCP retransmission timeout (RTO) is computed in a V2G entity, the RTO shall be lower than 400 ms.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the TCP retransmission timeout (RTO) calculated by any V2G entity adheres to the specified upper limit.

V2G20-2135.text: [V2G20-2135] Whenever a TCP retransmission timeout (RTO) is computed in a V2G entity, the RTO should be in the range of 50 ms (lower bound) and 110 ms (upper bound).

atoms.notes: This constraint applies to the computation of the TCP retransmission timeout (RTO) within any V2G entity.

V2G20-2136.text: [V2G20-2136] If the EVCC and the SECC agree to select "VehicleCheckIn" with setting value of 1 to "IntendedService", "VehicleCheckIn" request and response shall apply to selected "ParkingStatusService" as unique type of message exchange set.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures both EVCC and SECC have agreed on selecting 'VehicleCheckIn' with a specific setting value.
The EVCC shall send a 'VehicleCheckInReq' message when the conditions are met.
The SECC shall send a 'VehicleCheckInRes' message in response to the 'VehicleCheckInReq'.
Ensures the correct sequence of messages for the 'VehicleCheckIn' service.
Ensures that 'ParkingStatusService' is used uniquely when 'VehicleCheckIn' is selected.

V2G20-2137.text: [V2G20-2137] If the EVCC and the SECC agree to select "VehicleCheckOut" with setting value of 2 to "IntendedService", "VehicleCheckOut" request and response shall apply to selected "ParkingStatusService" as unique type of message exchange set.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures both EVCC and SECC have agreed on selecting 'VehicleCheckOut' with a specific setting value.
The EVCC shall send a VehicleCheckOut request when the conditions are met.
The SECC shall send a VehicleCheckOut response when the conditions are met.
The sequence constraint ensures that after a VehicleCheckOut request, a corresponding response is expected.
Ensures that 'VehicleCheckOut' applies uniquely to 'ParkingStatusService'.

V2G20-2139.text: [V2G20-2139] The duration element shall define the active period of time (s) for the respective parent element of EVPowerScheduleEntryType.

atoms.notes: The 'Duration' field within EVPowerScheduleEntryType must be non-negative and within a specified maximum limit.
When EVPowerScheduleEntryType is active, its 'Duration' must be greater than zero to define a valid active period.

V2G20-2140.text: [V2G20-2140] If AC was selected as energy transfer mode, the Power element shall define the maximum amount of apparent power to be drawn from the EV when the element of type EVPowerScheduleEntryType is active.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the requirement only applies when AC mode is selected.
The EVCC sets the Power element to the maximum apparent power when the EVPowerScheduleEntryType is active.
Ensures that the Power element is of type EVPowerScheduleEntryType.
This invariant ensures that while the EVPowerScheduleEntryType is active, the Power does not exceed the maximum apparent power.

V2G20-2141.text: [V2G20-2141] The power elements in the EVPowerScheduleType shall always be smaller or equal to zero as they communicate the discharging capabilities of the EV.

V2G20-2143.text: [V2G20-2143] The number of EVPriceRules shall not exceed value of MaximumSupportingPoints.

atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that the number of EVPriceRules does not exceed the MaximumSupportingPoints limit.

V2G20-2144.text: [V2G20-2144] An EVPriceRuleStack shall become active when the previous EVPriceRuleStack has expired, or when it is the first EVPriceRuleStack in the EVAbsolutePriceSchedule.

atoms.notes: This sequence constraint ensures that the current EVPriceRuleStack becomes active under specified conditions.
This guard checks if the previous EVPriceRuleStack has expired or if it's the first in the schedule.
This action specifies that the current EVPriceRuleStack should be activated.

V2G20-2145.text: [V2G20-2145] An EVPriceRuleStack expires when the current time is greater than the starting time of the EVPriceRuleStack plus the Duration.

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the EVPriceRuleStack is considered expired based on the specified condition.

V2G20-2146.text: [V2G20-2146] The first EVPriceRule in the EVPriceRuleStack shall start at the same time as the parent EVAbsolutePriceScheduleType's TimeAnchor.

atoms.notes: This ensures the first price rule starts at the same time as the schedule's anchor.

V2G20-2147.text: [V2G20-2147] The SECC and the EVCC shall implement this type as defined in Figure 144 and Table 141.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that both SECC and EVCC adhere to the specified type definition.

V2G20-2149.text: [V2G20-2149] The SECC and the EVCC shall implement this type as defined in Figure 145 and Table 142.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that both the SECC and EVCC implement the specified type as per the definitions provided in Figure 145 and Table 142.

V2G20-2150.text: [V2G20-2150] An EVPriceRule shall become active when the current power is at or below the PowerRangeStart value.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the current power is at or below the PowerRangeStart value.
This action specifies that the EVPriceRule should be activated when the guard condition is met.

atoms.expr: if CurrentPower <= PowerRangeStart then EVPriceRule.isActive == true
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that whenever the current power is at or below the PowerRangeStart value, the EVPriceRule is active.

V2G20-2152.text: [V2G20-2152] At least one active EVPriceRule shall have a PowerRangeStart with a value of zero.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that at least one active EVPriceRule has a PowerRangeStart value of zero, which is a global requirement across the session.

V2G20-2153.text: [V2G20-2153] PowerRangeStart shall be less than or equal to zero.

atoms.notes: This constraint applies to the SAP_Values message where PowerRangeStart is defined.

V2G20-2154.text: [V2G20-2154] PowerRangeStart values shall be unique within the same EVPriceRuleStack.

atoms.expr: forall i, j in EVPriceRuleStack where i != j: EVPriceRuleStack[i].PowerRangeStart != EVPriceRuleStack[j].PowerRangeStart
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that all PowerRangeStart values within the same EVPriceRuleStack are unique.

V2G20-2155.text: [V2G20-2155] The SECC and the EVCC shall implement this type as defined in Figure 155 and Table 146.

atoms.expr: The fields and their types shall be implemented as specified in Figure 155 and Table 146.
atoms.notes: This atom refers to the implementation of specific fields and their types as defined in the referenced figure and table.

V2G20-2156.text: [V2G20-2156] PowerRangeStart shall be greater than or equal to zero if the enclosing AbsolutePriceSchedule is used as a sub-element of a ChargingSchedule.

atoms.expr: PowerRangeStart >= 0 when AbsolutePriceSchedule is a sub-element of ChargingSchedule
atoms.notes: This constraint applies specifically when the AbsolutePriceSchedule is part of a ChargingSchedule.

V2G20-2157.text: [V2G20-2157] PowerRangeStart shall be less than or equal to zero if the enclosing AbsolutePriceSchedule is used as a sub-element of a DischargingSchedule.

atoms.expr: PowerRangeStart <= 0 when AbsolutePriceSchedule is within DischargingSchedule
atoms.notes: This constraint applies specifically when the AbsolutePriceSchedule is part of a DischargingSchedule.

V2G20-2158.text: [V2G20-2158] CarbonDioxideEmission and RenewableGenerationPercentage shall only be used when the enclosing AbsolutePriceSchedule is used as a sub-element of a ChargingSchedule and the PowerRangeStart is equal to zero.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the PowerRangeStart is equal to zero.
This constraint ensures that the AbsolutePriceSchedule is used as a sub-element of a ChargingSchedule.

atoms.expr: if (PowerRangeStart == 0 && AbsolutePriceSchedule is sub-element of ChargingSchedule) then (CarbonDioxideEmission is optional, RenewableGenerationPercentage is optional)
atoms.notes: This field constraint specifies the conditions under which CarbonDioxideEmission and RenewableGenerationPercentage can be used.
This guard checks if the overstay condition has been triggered.
The overstay detection should occur within a specified timeout period.
Once an overstay is detected, the SECC sends a notification message.
After sending the overstay notification, the next expected message could be an action request related to handling the overstay.
An invariant ensuring that once an overstay is detected, the system is in a state of handling the overstay.
Assumption that an overstay can only be detected during an active charging session.

V2G20-2162.text: [V2G20-2162] If more than one ScheduleTuple containing PriceLevelSchedule is sent to the EVCC, they shall have the same NumberOfPriceLevels and priceLevels inside different ScheduleTupleless shall correspond to the same energy price.

atoms.expr: forall ScheduleTuple_i, ScheduleTuple_j where i != j: forall k in [1..NumberOfPriceLevels]: ScheduleTuple_i.priceLevels[k].price == ScheduleTuple_j.priceLevels[k].price
atoms.notes: Ensures corresponding priceLevels across different ScheduleTuples have the same energy price.

V2G20-2163.text: [V2G20-2163] The TimeAnchor of a PriceLevelScheduleType element shall define a time that either is the present or some point in the near past.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the TimeAnchor is not set to a future time and is either the current time or a time in the recent past.

V2G20-2164.text: [V2G20-2164] The NumberOfPriceLevels element shall be defined as the overall number of distinct PriceLevel elements used across all PriceLevelSchedules under the ScheduleTupleType elements.

atoms.expr: NumberOfPriceLevels = count(distinct(PriceLevel)) for all PriceLevelSchedules under ScheduleTupleType
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the NumberOfPriceLevels accurately reflects the total number of unique PriceLevel values across all PriceLevelSchedules within the ScheduleTupleType.

V2G20-2165.text: [V2G20-2165] Both, EVCC and SECC shall support up to 100 price levels for the element NumberOfPriceLevels.

atoms.notes: This constraint applies globally to ensure both EVCC and SECC can handle up to 100 price levels.

V2G20-2166.text: [V2G20-2166] In case the value of NumberOfPriceLevels is equal to "0", the value of PriceLevel shall be "0".

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the NumberOfPriceLevels is equal to '0'.
This action sets the PriceLevel to '0' when the guard condition is met.
This field constraint ensures that if NumberOfPriceLevels is '0', then PriceLevel must also be '0'.

V2G20-2167.text: [V2G20-2167] A PriceLevelSchedule that is communicated as part of a ChargingScheduleType shall only present the price levels for power values that are equal to, or greater than 0 kW.

atoms.expr: forall p in PriceLevelSchedule.priceLevels: p.powerValue >= 0 kW
atoms.notes: Ensures that all price levels in the PriceLevelSchedule have power values that are non-negative.

V2G20-2168.text: [V2G20-2168] A PriceLevelSchedule that is communicated as part of a DischargingSchedule shall only present the price levels for all power levels that are less than 0 kW.

atoms.expr: forall p in PriceLevelSchedule.priceLevels: p.powerLevel < 0 kW
atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that all price levels within a PriceLevelSchedule included in a DischargingSchedule are for power levels less than 0 kW.

V2G20-2172.text: [V2G20-2172] The TimeAnchor of a PriceLevelScheduleType element shall define the point in time when the first PriceLevelScheduleEntry element starts to be active.

atoms.notes: Ensures that the first PriceLevelScheduleEntry starts at the defined TimeAnchor.

atoms.expr: forall entries in PriceLevelScheduleType: entries.TimeAnchor <= entries.PriceLevelScheduleEntry.start
atoms.notes: Ensures that for all entries in the PriceLevelScheduleType, the TimeAnchor precedes or coincides with the start of the first entry.

V2G20-2173.text: [V2G20-2173] The Duration element shall define the active period of time (in seconds) for the respective parent element of PriceLevelScheduleEntryType.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the Duration field within the PriceLevelScheduleEntryType message is correctly defined as a mandatory positive integer.
This invariant ensures that the Duration field always holds a positive value, reflecting an active period of time.

V2G20-2174.text: [V2G20-2174] The start time of each element in a list of consecutive PriceLevelScheduleEntryType elements shall be defined as the point in time when the previous element becomes inactive (see [V2G20-2173])

atoms.notes: This ensures that the start time of each PriceLevelScheduleEntry follows the end time of the previous entry, maintaining continuity.

atoms.expr: forall i in range(len(PriceLevelSchedule.PriceLevelScheduleEntry)): type(PriceLevelSchedule.PriceLevelScheduleEntry[i].StartDateTime) == DateTime and type(PriceLevelSchedule.PriceLevelScheduleEntry[i].EndDateTime) == DateTime
atoms.notes: Ensures that StartDateTime and EndDateTime fields are of type DateTime for all entries.
Ensures that the start time is always before or equal to the end time for each PriceLevelScheduleEntry.

V2G20-2175.text: [V2G20-2175] An EVCC shall set MaximumSupportingPoints to the maximum number of elements of PowerScheduleEntry, PriceRule and PriceLevelScheduleEntries it supports.

atoms.notes: This action ensures that the EVCC sets MaximumSupportingPoints correctly based on its support for various schedule entries.
Ensures that MaximumSupportingPoints is non-negative, reflecting a valid count of supported entries.
Ensures that MaximumSupportingPoints does not exceed the maximum number of entries the EVCC can support.

V2G20-2179.text: [V2G20-2179] In dynamic control mode the SECC shall provide the target setpoints for the power transfer by the means of EVSETargetActivePower and EVSETargetReactivePower in AC_ChargeLoopRes.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that we are operating in dynamic control mode.
The SECC provides target setpoints for active and reactive power in the AC_ChargeLoopRes message.

atoms.expr: AC_ChargeLoopRes.EVSETargetActivePower is mandatory AND AC_ChargeLoopRes.EVSETargetReactivePower is mandatory
atoms.notes: Both EVSETargetActivePower and EVSETargetReactivePower fields are mandatory in AC_ChargeLoopRes when in dynamic control mode.
The SECC has received an AC_ChargeLoopReq message.
The SECC sends an AC_ChargeLoopRes with ResponseCode Accepted.
The ResponseCode field in AC_ChargeLoopRes is mandatory.
The response must be sent within the specified timeout period.
After sending AC_ChargeLoopRes, the next allowed request is AC_ChargeLoopReq.

V2G20-2181.text: [V2G20-2181] During charging the SECC shall always respect the limits defined by EVMaximumChargePower, EVMaximumChargeCurrent, EVMaximumVoltage and EVMaximumVoltage.

atoms.expr: SECCChargePower <= EVMaximumChargePower AND SECCChargeCurrent <= EVMaximumChargeCurrent AND SECCVoltage <= EVMaximumVoltage
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the SECC respects the limits provided by the EV during the entire charging session.

V2G20-2182.text: [V2G20-2182] During discharging the SECC shall always respect the limits defined by EVMaximumDischargePower, EVMaximumDischargeCurrent, EVMaximumVoltage and EVMaximumVoltage.

atoms.expr: SECCDischargePower <= EVMaximumDischargePower AND SECCDischargeCurrent <= EVMaximumDischargeCurrent AND SECCVoltage <= EVMaximumVoltage
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that during discharging, the SECC never exceeds the limits specified by the EV.

V2G20-2183.text: [V2G20-2183] In a DC_ChargeLoopReq the EVCC shall either provide a EVTargetVoltage or EVTargetCurrent value.

atoms.expr: (EVTargetVoltage is not null) OR (EVTargetCurrent is not null)
atoms.notes: This ensures that at least one of the two fields is provided in the message.

V2G20-2184.text: [V2G20-2184] If the EVCC provides an EVTargetVoltage value, the EVTargetVoltage shall be defined in such a way, that it is logically consistent with the reported EVPresentVoltage.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC has provided an EVTargetVoltage value.

atoms.expr: EVTargetVoltage is logically consistent with EVPresentVoltage
atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that the EVTargetVoltage value is logically consistent with the EVPresentVoltage value reported by the EVCC.

V2G20-2185.text: [V2G20-2185] The SECC shall adjust the voltage on the EVSE side in such a way, that the reported EVPresentVoltage matches the requested EVTargetVoltage as rapidly and closely as technically possible.

atoms.notes: The SECC must actively adjust the voltage.
The difference between EVPresentVoltage and EVTargetVoltage should be minimized.
The adjustment should happen within a specified timeout.
Assumes that the adjustment is technically feasible given the hardware constraints.

V2G20-2186.text: [V2G20-2186] If the EVCC provides an EVTargetCurrent value, the EVTargetCurrent shall be defined in such a way, that it is logically consistent with the reported EVSEPresentCurrent.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC has provided an EVTargetCurrent value.

atoms.expr: EVTargetCurrent is logically consistent with EVSEPresentCurrent
atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that the EVTargetCurrent value provided by the EVCC is logically consistent with the EVSEPresentCurrent reported by the SECC.
This invariant ensures that throughout the session, the EVTargetCurrent does not exceed the EVSEPresentCurrent by more than a specified tolerance to maintain logical consistency.

V2G20-2187.text: [V2G20-2187] The SECC shall adjust the current on the EVSE side in such a way, that the reported EVSEPresentCurrent matches the requested EVTargetCurrent as rapidly and closely as technically possible.

atoms.notes: The SECC adjusts its current output to match the EV's target current.
The EVSEPresentCurrent should be as close as possible to the EVTargetCurrent.
Throughout the session, the difference between EVSEPresentCurrent and EVTargetCurrent should be minimized within a technical tolerance ε.
The adjustment of the current by the SECC should happen within a specified timeout period.

V2G20-2188.text: [V2G20-2188] In its attempt to reach an EVTargetVoltage or EVTargetCurrent setpoint, the SECC shall never initiate an EVSE behavior which would violate any of the communicated and applicable limits (maximum and minimum values; for example, see [V2G20-2181] and [V2G20-2182]).

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the SECC's behavior always respects the maximum and minimum limits communicated by the EVCC.
This guard ensures that before initiating any new behavior, the SECC checks against the communicated limits.
Assumes that the EVCC has communicated valid limits to the SECC.

V2G20-2189.text: [V2G20-2189] The AvailableEnergy element shall only be included in instances of PowerScheduleType which are describing charging limits within a ChargingSchedule element.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the AvailableEnergy element is only included when the PowerScheduleType describes charging limits and is part of a ChargingSchedule.

V2G20-2190.text: [V2G20-2190] If used in the context of a ChargingSchedule element then the AvailableEnergy element shall only contain values greater than zero.

atoms.expr: AvailableEnergy > 0 when AvailableEnergy is within a ChargingSchedule element
atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that the AvailableEnergy field, when present in a ChargingSchedule, contains positive values.

V2G20-2191.text: [V2G20-2191] In dynamic control mode the objective of the energy transfer plan shall be that at the end of the service session the EVTargetEnergyRequest will be less than or equal to zero.

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that by the end of the service session, the EV's target energy request is met or exceeded.

V2G20-2192.text: [V2G20-2192] If the PowerDeliveryReq received has ChargeProgress = "Standby" and ServiceName = AC or AC_BPT in Table 204 was selected, the next allowed request shall be AC_ChargeLoopReq and the V2G_SECC_Sequence_Timeout is set according to Table 216.

atoms.notes: Checks if the received PowerDeliveryReq meets the specified conditions.
Sets the timeout according to the values specified in Table 216.

V2G20-2193.text: [V2G20-2193] If the EVCC wants to enter a standby phase and received the AC_ChargeLoopRes with "ResponseCode = OK, the EVCC shall send a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress = "Standby" within V2G_EVCC_Sequence_Performance_Timeout according to Table 215.

atoms.notes: Checks if the EVCC wants to enter standby phase and has received an AC_ChargeLoopRes with ResponseCode OK.

V2G20-2195.text: [V2G20-2195] If the EVCC wants to enter a standby phase and received the DC_ChargeLoopRes with "ResponseCode = OK", the EVCC shall send a PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress = "Standby" within V2G_EVCC_Sequence_Performance_Timeout according to Table 215.

atoms.notes: Checks if EVCC wants to enter standby phase and received correct response code.
EVCC sends PowerDeliveryReq with ChargeProgress set to Standby.

V2G20-2200.text: [V2G20-2200] If [V2G20-728] applies, the EVCC can establish a new V2G communication session by applying [V2G20-014].

V2G20-2201.text: [V2G20-2201] If the ResponseCode contains a value starting with WARNING, the EVCC shall take appropriate actions as defined for that particular WARNING response for that particular message.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the ResponseCode starts with 'WARNING'.
The EVCC shall take the appropriate action based on the specific WARNING response code.

atoms.notes: Ensures that ResponseCode is a mandatory string field in all messages.

V2G20-2202.text: [V2G20-2202] If the SECC sends a ResponseCode containing a value starting with WARNING all mandatory parameters shall be filled as defined for that particular WARNING response for that particular message.

atoms.notes: Ensures all mandatory parameters are filled according to the specific WARNING response.

V2G20-2203.text: [V2G20-2223] After receiving the CertificateInstallationReq, if an issue was detected with the provided OEM provisioning certificate chain, the SECC shall respond with a CertificateInstallationRes with EVSEProcessing set to "Finished" and ResponseCode starting with "WARNING", specifying the detected issue with the provided OEMProvisioningCertificate chain (refer to [V2G20-2203], [V2G20-1412], [V2G20-2204] and [V2G20-2205] for further details of the ResponseCode to be provided) within V2G_SECC_Msg_Performance_Time according to Table 215.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the SECC has received the CertificateInstallationReq and detected an issue with the OEM provisioning certificate chain.

Ensures that sending CertificateInstallationRes is the next allowed action after detecting an issue.

V2G20-2204.text: [V2G20-2223] After receiving the CertificateInstallationReq, if an issue was detected with the provided OEM provisioning certificate chain, the SECC shall respond with a CertificateInstallationRes with EVSEProcessing set to "Finished" and ResponseCode starting with "WARNING", specifying the detected issue with the provided OEMProvisioningCertificate chain (refer to [V2G20-2203], [V2G20-1412], [V2G20-2204] and [V2G20-2205] for further details of the ResponseCode to be provided) within V2G_SECC_Msg_Performance_Time according to Table 215.

V2G20-2205.text: [V2G20-2223] After receiving the CertificateInstallationReq, if an issue was detected with the provided OEM provisioning certificate chain, the SECC shall respond with a CertificateInstallationRes with EVSEProcessing set to "Finished" and ResponseCode starting with "WARNING", specifying the detected issue with the provided OEMProvisioningCertificate chain (refer to [V2G20-2203], [V2G20-1412], [V2G20-2204] and [V2G20-2205] for further details of the ResponseCode to be provided) within V2G_SECC_Msg_Performance_Time according to Table 215.

V2G20-2206.text: [V2G20-2206] The message "CertificateInstallationRes" shall contain the ResponseCode "WARNING_NoContractMatchingPCIDFound" if the SA(s) indicate to the SECC that after a complete search, no contract could be found for the PCID contained in the OEM provisioning certificate received in the OEMProvisioningCertificate chain contained in the CertificateInstallationReq message.

V2G20-2207.text: [V2G20-2207] The message "CertificateInstallationRes" shall contain the ResponseCode "WARNING_NoCertificateAvailable" if a new contract certificate cannot be retrieved from secondary actor within V2G_SECC_Msg_Performance_Time according to Table 215.

V2G20-2208.text: [V2G20-2208] The message CertificateInstallationRes shall contain the ResponseCode "WARNING_eMSPUnknown" if the SECC does not recognize any one (or more) of the eMSPs indicated by the EMAID included in the PrioritizedEMAIDs list it received in CertificateInstallationReq message.

This ensures that the AuthorizationRes message is sent after receiving the AuthorizationReq message.

V2G20-2210.text: [V2G20-2210] The message AuthorizationRes shall contain the ResponseCode "WARNING_ContractCancelled" if the SECC received the information (potentially from SA; it is not in the scope of this document to define how the SECC received this information) that the contract associated with the ContractCertificate it received in AuthorizationReq message, in attribute ContractSignatureCertChain, has been cancelled.

This guard ensures that the ContractSignatureCertChain was provided in the AuthorizationReq message.
This assumption states that the SECC has received the necessary information about the contract cancellation, potentially from the Service Authority (SA).

V2G20-2211.text: [V2G20-2211] The message AuthorizationRes shall contain the ResponseCode "WARNING_eMSPUnknown" if the SECC does not recognize the eMSP indicated by the EMAID included in the ContractCertificate it received in AuthorizationReq message, in attribute ContractSignatureCertChain.

V2G20-2212.text: If any of the aforementioned verifications and validations fail, the SECC shall consider the contract certificate as invalid, and shall not use said contract certificate any further – see [V2G20-2212], [V2G20-2213], [V2G20-2214] and [V2G20-2215].

V2G20-2214.text: If any of the aforementioned verifications and validations fail, the SECC shall consider the contract certificate as invalid, and shall not use said contract certificate any further – see [V2G20-2212], [V2G20-2213], [V2G20-2214] and [V2G20-2215].

atoms.expr: VerificationFailed || ValidationFailed -> ReferTo(V2G20-2212, V2G20-2213, V2G20-2214, V2G20-2215)
atoms.notes: Assumes that the conditions for failure are defined in the referenced requirements.

V2G20-2215.text: If any of the aforementioned verifications and validations fail, the SECC shall consider the contract certificate as invalid, and shall not use said contract certificate any further – see [V2G20-2212], [V2G20-2213], [V2G20-2214] and [V2G20-2215].

atoms.notes: Checks if the SECC provided a Receipt in the last ChargeLoopRes.
The EVCC includes the Receipt from the last ChargeLoopRes in the MeteringConfirmationReq.

V2G20-2238.text: [V2G20-2238] If the OEM wants their EVs to access CSO's secure WLAN for EV-EVSE charging communications, the WLAN STA (see ISO 15118-8 for details) in the OEM's EV shall implement all specifications in this subclause and the subclauses within.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the WLAN STA is implemented in the EV if the OEM wants to use the CSO's secure WLAN.
The EVCC must implement all specifications related to the WLAN STA as defined in this subclause and its subclauses.
It is assumed that the CSO's secure WLAN is accessible for EV-EVSE charging communications.
The invariant ensures that the WLAN STA in the EV remains compliant with the specified standards throughout the session.

V2G20-2239.text: [V2G20-2239] It is up to the CSOs discretion whether to allow an EV that does not support the required security for WLAN to access the CSO's secure WLAN for EV-EVSE charging communications.

atoms.notes: This assumption captures the CSO's policy decision regarding WLAN security requirements.
This guard ensures that if the CSO requires secure WLAN and the EV does not support it, the transition cannot proceed.
This guard allows the transition to proceed even if the EV does not support secure WLAN, provided the CSO allows insecure access.
This invariant ensures that if the CSO requires secure WLAN, the EV must support it throughout the session.

V2G20-2240.text: [V2G20-2240] It is up to the OEM's discretion whether to allow an EV that supports security for WLAN to access a CSO's unsecured WLAN for EV-EVSE charging communications.

atoms.notes: This assumption reflects the OEM's discretion regarding WLAN support.
The EVCC may attempt to access a secure WLAN if it supports both WLAN and its security.
The EVCC may attempt to access an unsecured WLAN if it supports WLAN but not its security.
The sequence constraint ensures that after sending a WLAN access request, the EVCC expects a response.
If the WLAN access status is not granted, the charging communication method cannot be set to WLAN.

V2G20-2241.text: [V2G20-2241] A V2G entity shall implement IEEE 802.1X.

atoms.notes: This atom represents the assumption that both the EVCC and SECC must support IEEE 802.1X as per the requirement.

V2G20-2242.text: [V2G20-2242] IETF RFC 3748 shall be used as the encapsulation of IEEE 802.1X.

atoms.notes: This assumption ensures that IETF RFC 3748 is used for encapsulating IEEE 802.1X communications.

V2G20-2243.text: [V2G20-2243] Remote authentication dial-in user service (RADIUS) as specified by IETF RFC 3579 shall be used as "pass-through peer" implementation of IETF RFC 3748 by the CSO/PE operator.

atoms.notes: This assumption captures the requirement that the CSO/PE operator uses RADIUS as a pass-through peer implementation of EAP.
Ensures that the EAP method type used is consistent with RADIUS as specified by IETF RFC 3579.
Ensures that the EAP peer implementation conforms to the specifications outlined in IETF RFC 3748.

V2G20-2244.text: [V2G20-2244] The V2G entity shall use EAP extension EAP-TLS, as specified by IETF RFC 5216.

atoms.notes: This atom assumes that the implementation of EAP-TLS conforms to the specifications provided by IETF RFC 5216.

V2G20-2246.text: [V2G20-2246] RADIUS accounting requirements specified in IETF RFC 2866 shall be implemented.

atoms.notes: This atom assumes that the SECC supports RADIUS authentication and accounting as per IETF RFC 2866.
The SECC shall implement the RADIUS accounting requirements as specified in IETF RFC 2866.
Throughout the session, the SECC must ensure compliance with the RADIUS accounting requirements specified in IETF RFC 2866.

V2G20-2247.text: [V2G20-2247] When the EVCC uses a wireless medium to establish a physical connection to an AP (see ISO 15118-8 for details), the EV's WLAN STA (see ISO 15118-8 for details) shall use WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise according to IEEE 802.1X.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the requirement only applies when a wireless medium is used.
The EVCC must configure its WLAN STA to use either WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise security protocols.
It is assumed that the EVCC's WLAN STA is compliant with IEEE 802.1X standards.

V2G20-2248.text: [V2G20-2248] When the CSO offers a wireless medium to establish a physical connection to an AP (see ISO 15118-8 for details), the CSO shall use WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise according to IEEE802.1X.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the CSO is offering a wireless medium.
The SECC shall use WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise according to IEEE802.1X when a wireless medium is offered.
It is assumed that the environment complies with IEEE802.1X standards.

V2G20-2249.text: [V2G20-2249] If the EVCC uses WPA3-Enterprise, its STA device shall set protected management frames (PMF) to required.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC is using WPA3-Enterprise security profile.
This action specifies that the EVCC's STA device should set PMF to required when using WPA3-Enterprise.

V2G20-2250.text: [V2G20-2250] If the CSO uses WPA3-Enterprise, its AP shall set protected management frames (PMF) to be required.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the Charging Station Operator (CSO) uses WPA3-Enterprise security policy.
This action specifies that the Access Point (AP) shall set Protected Management Frames (PMF) to be required when WPA3-Enterprise is used.

atoms.expr: if CSO_Security_Policy == WPA3_Enterprise then PMF_Required == true
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that whenever WPA3-Enterprise is used by the CSO, PMF is always required.

V2G20-2251.text: [V2G20-2251] If the EVCC uses WPA3-Enterprise, its WLAN STA shall not support WPA3-Enterprise transition mode.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that if the EVCC uses WPA3-Enterprise, it does not support the transition mode.
This assumption sets the context for the requirement by assuming the EVCC uses WPA3-Enterprise.

V2G20-2252.text: [V2G20-2252] If the CSO uses WPA3-Enterprise, its AP shall not support WPA3-Enterprise transition mode.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the CSO is configured to use WPA3-Enterprise.
This invariant ensures that if WPA3-Enterprise is used, transition mode is not supported.

V2G20-2253.text: [V2G20-2253] Regardless of WPA3-Enterprise is used or WPA2-Enterprise is used, the EV's WLAN STA (see ISO 15118-8 for details) shall implement MAC address randomization.

atoms.notes: This action ensures that the EV's WLAN STA implements MAC address randomization regardless of whether WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise is used.
This guard checks if either WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise is being used by the EV.
This invariant ensures that MAC address randomization is always implemented by the EV's WLAN STA.

V2G20-2254.text: [V2G20-2254] Regardless of WPA3-Enterprise is used or WPA2-Enterprise is used, the EV's WLAN STA (see ISO 15118-8 for details) shall implement "server certificate validation" to ensure that the AP that the EVCC connects to is a valid and trustworthy WLAN AP.

atoms.notes: This action ensures that the EVCC's WLAN STA implements server certificate validation.
This guard checks if either WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise is being used by the WLAN STA.
This invariant ensures that the WLAN AP connected to by the EVCC is always validated as valid and trustworthy.
This assumption considers that the WLAN AP supports server certificate validation, which is necessary for the EVCC to validate the AP.

V2G20-2255.text: [V2G20-2255] The CSO shall provide an SECC certificate, as defined in Annex B, to the EVCC so that the EVCC can authenticate the CSO's authentication server.

atoms.notes: The SECC must send a CertificateInstallationRes message containing the SECCCertificate.

atoms.expr: SECCCertificate is mandatory and conforms to Annex B
atoms.notes: The SECCCertificate field must be present and adhere to the specifications in Annex B.

atoms.expr: EVCC receives CertificateInstallationRes with valid SECCCertificate
atoms.notes: The EVCC must receive a valid SECCCertificate within the CertificateInstallationRes message.

atoms.expr: EVCC authenticates CSO's authentication server using SECCCertificate
atoms.notes: The EVCC uses the received SECCCertificate to authenticate the CSO's authentication server.

atoms.expr: Annex B defines the structure and requirements for SECCCertificate
atoms.notes: It is assumed that Annex B provides the necessary definitions for the SECCCertificate.

V2G20-2256.text: [V2G20-2256] The EVCC shall disable user override of server certificate (UOSC).

atoms.notes: This action ensures that the EVCC does not allow the user to override the server certificate validation process.
This invariant ensures that the UOSC flag remains disabled throughout the session.

V2G20-2257.text: [V2G20-2257] The EVCC shall authenticate CSO's authentication server with the certificate provided by the CSO's authentication server.

atoms.notes: The EVCC performs the authentication process using the certificate provided by the CSO's authentication server.
Before authentication, the EVCC must have received a non-null certificate from the CSO's authentication server.
Throughout the session, the CSO's authentication server certificate must remain valid for the EVCC to trust it.
It is assumed that the SECC will provide a valid certificate from the CSO's authentication server to the EVCC.

V2G20-2258.text: [V2G20-2258] The EVCC shall validate the provided certificate per [V2G20-1001] (with the SECC certificate profile as defined in Annex B).

atoms.notes: The validation process should follow the rules specified in [V2G20-1001] and use the certificate profile defined in Annex B.
Ensure that the certificate profile used for validation matches the SECC certificate profile as defined in Annex B.
Assume that the SECC certificate profile as defined in Annex B is valid and correctly implemented by the SECC.

V2G20-2259.text: [V2G20-2259] If the EVCC is unable to successfully authenticate the CSO’s authentication server, it shall decline to establish a wireless connection with the CSO’s access point.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the authentication process did not result in a successful status.
This action represents the EVCC declining to establish a wireless connection due to unsuccessful authentication.
This sequence constraint ensures that after an unsuccessful authentication, the next allowed action is to not connect wirelessly.
This invariant ensures that the wireless connection remains unestablished when authentication fails.

V2G20-2260.text: [V2G20-2260] When the CSO’s authentication server requests EVCC to present its certificate to authenticate itself, the EVCC shall provide its vehicle certificate.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the SECC's AuthenticationRequest message requests a certificate from the EVCC.
This action specifies that the EVCC must send an AuthenticationRes message containing its vehicle certificate.
This field constraint ensures that the VehicleCertificate field is mandatory in the AuthenticationRes message sent by the EVCC.
This sequence constraint ensures that the AuthenticationRes message is sent by the EVCC after receiving the AuthenticationReq message from the SECC.

V2G20-2261.text: [V2G20-2261] The CSO’s authentication server shall authenticate the EVCC using the certificate provided by the EVCC.

atoms.notes: The SECC's CSO authentication server performs the authentication process.
The EVCC certificate must be provided for authentication to proceed.
The EVCC certificate must be of type X509 as per the standard.
After successful authentication, the session's Authentication_Status should reflect this.
It is assumed that the CSO's authentication server is operational and capable of performing authentication tasks.

V2G20-2262.text: [V2G20-2262] The CSO’s authentication server shall validate the provided certificate per [V2G20-1001] (with the vehicle certificate profile as defined in Annex B).

atoms.notes: The SECC's CSO authentication server performs the validation.
The vehicle certificate must conform to the profile specified in Annex B.
Assumes that the certificate validation rules are defined by V2G20-1001.

V2G20-2263.text: [V2G20-2263] If the CSO’s authentication server is unable to successfully authenticate the EV, it shall decline establishing a wireless connection with the EV.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the CSO's authentication server was unable to authenticate the EV.
This action specifies that the SECC shall decline establishing a wireless connection with the EV.
This sequence constraint ensures that after failing authentication, the next state should be one where no wireless connection is established.
This assumption states that the CSO's authentication server is functional and can provide a response.

V2G20-2264.text: [V2G20-2264] The CSO shall utilize the cipher suites as specified by Table 6 for EAP-TLS.

atoms.notes: The specific values from Table 6 need to be enumerated.
This action ensures that the SECC selects and uses the appropriate cipher suite as defined in Table 6.

atoms.expr: CipherSuite must be one of the values specified in Table 6 throughout the session
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that once a cipher suite is selected, it remains consistent with the specifications in Table 6 for the duration of the session.

V2G20-2265.text: [V2G20-2265] The EVCC shall utilize the cipher suite as specified by Table 6 for EAP-TLS.

atoms.notes: The specific value should be replaced with the actual cipher suite value from Table 6.
This action ensures that the EVCC sets the CipherSuite field according to the values specified in Table 6.

atoms.expr: CipherSuite must be one of the values specified in Table 6
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that throughout the session, the CipherSuite used by the EVCC adheres to the specifications in Table 6.

V2G20-2266.text: [V2G20-2266] The CSO shall utilize the (elliptic curve) ECs as specified by Table 7 for EAP.

atoms.notes: The CSO must use the elliptic curves specified in Table 7 for EAP.

V2G20-2267.text: [V2G20-2267] The EVCC shall utilize the (elliptic curve) ECs as specified by Table 7 for EAP-TLS.

atoms.notes: The elliptic curves used in EAP-TLS must be one of those specified in Table 7.
Before sending EAP-TLS messages, the EVCC must ensure that the selected elliptic curve is compliant with Table 7.

V2G20-2268.text: [V2G20-2268] The CSO shall utilize ECDHE for EAP.

atoms.notes: This atom specifies that the SECC must use ECDHE as the EAP method.

V2G20-2269.text: [V2G20-2269] The EVCC shall utilize ECDHE for EAP.

atoms.notes: This atom specifies that the EVCC must use ECDHE method for EAP.

V2G20-2270.text: [V2G20-2270] The CSO shall utilize the signature algorithm as specified by Table 8 for EAP.

atoms.notes: The CSO must use a signature algorithm defined in Table 8 when constructing EAP messages.

atoms.expr: set SignatureAlgorithm to value from Table 8
atoms.notes: The SECC must set the SignatureAlgorithm field according to the values specified in Table 8.

V2G20-2271.text: [V2G20-2271] The EVCC shall utilize the signature algorithm as specified by Table 8 for EAP.

atoms.notes: This requirement applies when the EAP method is either EAP-TLS or EAP-TTLS.

atoms.expr: SignatureAlgorithm remains consistent throughout the session
atoms.notes: Once a SignatureAlgorithm is chosen, it should not change during the same session.

V2G20-2272.text: [V2G20-2272] The message "DC_ChargeParameterDiscoveryRes" shall contain the ResponseCode "FAILED_WrongChargeParameter" if the content of attribute "EV_EnergyTransferParameter" in the DC_ChargeParameterDiscoveryReq message is not valid, for example, wrong parameter set is provided, one or multiple parameters cannot be interpreted.

atoms.expr: EV_EnergyTransferParameter is mandatory and has specific valid values
atoms.notes: This ensures that the EV_EnergyTransferParameter field is mandatory and specifies its valid values.

atoms.expr: if EV_EnergyTransferParameter is not valid then ResponseCode == 'FAILED_WrongChargeParameter'
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that whenever the EV_EnergyTransferParameter is invalid, the ResponseCode is set to 'FAILED_WrongChargeParameter'.

V2G20-2273.text: [V2G20-2273] If PLC communication according to ISO 15118-3 is applied, the SDP client in the EVCC shall use SECC discovery message with the payload type SDPRequestPayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: This guard checks if PLC communication according to ISO 15118-3 is being used.
The SDP client in the EVCC sends a SECC discovery message.
The payload type of the SECC discovery message must be SDPRequestPayloadID.

V2G20-2274.text: [V2G20-2274] If PLC communication according to ISO 15118-3 is applied, the SDP client in the EVCC shall only accept SDP response messages with the payload type SDPResponsePayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: Ensures the SDP response message has the correct payload type when PLC communication is used.
The SDP client in the EVCC shall only accept SDP response messages with the correct payload type.

V2G20-2275.text: [V2G20-2275] If the SDP server shall handle charging services with PLC (according to ISO 15118-3), the SDP server shall accept SECC discovery request messages with payload type SDPRequestPayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the payload type is correctly identified as SDPRequestPayloadID.
The SECC shall accept the discovery request message if the payload type is SDPRequestPayloadID.
Assumes that the SDP server supports charging services with PLC according to ISO 15118-3.
Ensures that SDPRequestPayloadID is a mandatory field in the SECC discovery request message.

V2G20-2276.text: [V2G20-2276] An SDP server which is used for PLC communication according to ISO 15118-3 shall use SECC discovery response message for PLC with payload type SDPResponsePayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: Ensures that the payload type is correctly identified as SDPResponsePayloadID.
The SECC sends a discovery response message for PLC communication.
The SDPResponsePayloadID field must be present and mandatory in the SECC discovery response message.
Assumes that the PLC communication is conducted according to the specifications in ISO 15118-3.

V2G20-2277.text: [V2G20-2277] If wireless communication according to ISO 15118-8 is applied the SDP client in the EVCC shall use SECC discovery message for wireless communication with the payload type SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the communication medium is wireless and follows ISO 15118-8 standard.
The SDP client in the EVCC sends a SECC discovery message when wireless communication is used.
The payload type in the SECC discovery message should be SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID as per Table 14.

V2G20-2278.text: [V2G20-2278] If wireless communication according to ISO 15118-8 is applied, the SDP client in the EVCC shall only accept SDP response messages with the payload type SDPResponseWirelessPayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: Checks if the communication medium is wireless as per ISO 15118-8.
Ensures that the SDP response message has the correct payload type when wireless communication is used.
The SDP client in the EVCC shall only accept SDP response messages with the specified payload type.

V2G20-2279.text: [V2G20-2279] If the SDP server shall handle charging services with wireless communication (according to ISO 15118-8), the SDP server shall accept SECC discovery request messages with payload type SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID (see Table 14).

V2G20-2280.text: [V2G20-2280] An SDP server which is used for wireless communication according to ISO 15118-8 shall use SECC discovery response message for wireless communication with payload type SDPResponseWirelessPayloadID (see Table 14).

atoms.notes: Ensures the correct communication mode and protocol are being used.
The SECC sends the SDP discovery response with the specified payload type.
Ensures the SDPResponseWirelessPayloadID field is present and mandatory in the message.

atoms.expr: SDP server is compliant with ISO 15118-8
atoms.notes: Assumes the SDP server adheres to the standards defined in ISO 15118-8.

V2G20-2281.text: [V2G20-2281] If an EVCC cannot provide data for the EVID, the EVID shall be set to "ZZ00000"

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC cannot provide data for the EVID.
This action sets the EVID to 'ZZ00000' when the EVCC cannot provide data for it.

V2G20-2284.text: [V2G20-2284] For wireless communication the SDP client shall send the SECC discovery request message with the payload type SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID as defined in Figure 20.

atoms.notes: The SDP client sends the SECC discovery request message.
The PayloadType field in the SECC discovery request message must be set to SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID.
This requirement assumes that the communication mode is wireless.

V2G20-2285.text: [V2G20-2285] For wireless communication an SDP client shall send the payload in the order as shown in Figure 3.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the SDP client sends the payload fields in the specific order defined by Figure 3 for wireless communication.

V2G20-2286.text: [V2G20-2286] For wireless communication the SDP client shall send the SECC discovery request message with the payload type value SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID as defined in Table 14, Figure 3 and Figure 4.

atoms.notes: The SDP client is responsible for sending the SECC discovery request message.
The PayloadType field in the SECC discovery request message must be set to SDPRequestWirelessPayloadID.
This requirement assumes that the communication medium is wireless.

V2G20-2287.text: [V2G20-2287] The SDP client shall stop sending SECC discovery request messages after a valid SECC discovery response message has been received with "DiagStatus" = "finished with EVSEID" or "finished without EVSEID".

atoms.expr: DiagStatus == 'finished with EVSEID' OR DiagStatus == 'finished without EVSEID'
atoms.notes: This guard checks if the received SECC discovery response contains a DiagStatus indicating completion.
The SDP client stops sending SECC discovery request messages once the guard condition is met.
After receiving a valid SECC discovery response with the specified DiagStatus, no further SECC discovery requests are allowed.

V2G20-2288.text: [V2G20-2288] For wireless communication the SDP client shall wait at least 250 ms before sending the next SECC discovery request message after an SECC discovery response message has been received with the payload parameter "DiagStatus" = "ongoing".

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the DiagStatus in the SECC discovery response is 'ongoing'.
The EVCC must wait at least 250ms before sending the next SECC discovery request.
This sequence constraint ensures that after receiving a SECC discovery response, the EVCC waits for 250ms before sending the next SECC discovery request.

V2G20-2289.text: [V2G20-2289] For wireless communication the SDP client shall set the timeout V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timeout to the value as defined in Table 221, reset the V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timer and start monitoring the V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timer when a successful TCP/TLS connection is established.

atoms.notes: The value should be taken from Table 221 as specified.
The timer needs to be reset upon establishing a successful TCP/TLS connection.
Monitoring of the timer starts after resetting it.
These actions are conditional on a successful TCP/TLS connection being established.

V2G20-2290.text: [V2G20-2290] A SDP server for wireless communication in a single SECC architecture shall reply to any SECC discovery request message with an SECC discovery response message.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the SECC has received a SECC discovery request message.
The SECC must send an SECC discovery response message in response to a SECC discovery request.
Ensures that the SECC discovery response is the next allowed message following a SECC discovery request.
Assumes that the SDP server for wireless communication is operational within the SECC architecture.

V2G20-2292.text: [V2G20-2292] For wireless communication the SDP server shall send the SECC discovery response message with the payload type value SDPResponseWirelessPayloadID as defined in

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the SECC sends the SDP discovery response message with the correct payload type for wireless communication.
This atom ensures that the action only applies when the communication mode is set to wireless.

atoms.expr: PayloadType is mandatory and of type SDPResponseWirelessPayloadID
atoms.notes: This atom specifies the field constraint for the PayloadType in the SDPDiscoveryRes message.

V2G20-2293.text: [V2G20-2293] For wireless communication the SDP server shall send the SECC discovery response message with the payload as defined in Table 26 and Table 27.

atoms.notes: The SDP server sends the SECC discovery response message.
The payload of the SECC discovery response message must be as defined in Table 26 and Table 27.
This requirement only applies when the communication medium is wireless.

V2G20-2294.text: [V2G20-2294] For wireless communication an SDP server shall send the payload in the order as shown in Table 26 and Table 27.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the SDP server sends the payload in the specified order as defined in Table 26 and Table 27 for wireless communication.

V2G20-2295.text: [V2G20-2295] If the EVCC receives an SDP response message with parameter DiagStatus equal to "Ongoing" for the first time it shall start the timer V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timer and wait

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the DiagStatus parameter in the SDP response is 'Ongoing'.
The EVCC starts the V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timer when the DiagStatus is 'Ongoing' for the first time.
After starting the timer, the EVCC waits for the V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timer to expire or be reset.

V2G20-2296.text: [V2G20-2296] If [V2G20-2295] applies, the EVCC shall stop and then restart the SDP process when V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timer is equal or larger than V2G_EVCC_Ongoing_Timeout and no parameter EVSE_Processing equal to "Finished" has been received.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the ongoing timer exceeds the timeout and no 'Finished' processing status has been received.
The EVCC shall stop and then restart the SDP process under the specified conditions.
This assumption ensures that the context of [V2G20-2295] is considered for the current requirement.

V2G20-2298.text: [V2G20-2298] The EVCC shall set the timeout V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timeout to the value as defined in Table 221, reset the V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timer and start monitoring the V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Timer when a successful TCP/TLS connection has been established.

atoms.notes: The value from Table 221 should be used for setting the timeout.
These actions are conditional on a successful TCP/TLS connection.

V2G20-2300.text: [V2G20-2300] The SECC shall stop waiting for SessionSetupReq and stop monitoring the V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Timer when V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Timer is smaller than V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Performance_Time and a SessionSetupRes message was received.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the communication setup timer is less than the performance time.
This guard ensures that a SessionSetupRes message has been received.
The SECC stops waiting for a SessionSetupReq message.
The SECC stops monitoring the V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Timer.

V2G20-2301.text: [V2G20-4000] If EVCC is using ServiceName = DC_ACDP, the following requirements are not applicable: [V2G20-1540], [V2G20-2301], [V2G20-2624] and [V2G20-1028].

atoms.expr: IF ServiceName == 'DC_ACDP' THEN NOT (V2G20-1540 OR V2G20-2301 OR V2G20-2624 OR V2G20-1028)
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that if the EVCC is using DC_ACDP service, the specified requirements are not applicable.

V2G20-2303.text: [V2G20-2303] The SECC shall set the timeout V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Performance_Time the value as defined in Table 221, reset the V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Timer and start monitoring the V2G_SECC_CommunicationSetup_Timer when a successful TCP/TLS connection has been established.

atoms.notes: The value is taken from Table 221 as specified in the requirement.
The timer is reset upon a successful TCP/TLS connection.
Monitoring of the timer begins after resetting it.

V2G20-2307.text: [V2G20-2307] A V2GTP entity shall use the definitions as defined in Table 13 and Table 14.

atoms.expr: All fields used by V2GTP entities comply with the definitions in Table 13 and Table 14.
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that all fields utilized by V2GTP entities adhere to the specifications provided in Table 13 and Table 14.

V2G20-2308.text: [V2G20-2308] The XML schema with the namespace "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:AC" shall be used for encoding and decoding EXI streams sent or received with Part20ACMainstreamPayloadID and defined in 8.3.4.4.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the correct XML schema namespace is used for encoding and decoding EXI streams.
This atom specifies that the XML schema defined in section 8.3.4.4 shall be used for encoding and decoding EXI streams.

V2G20-2309.text: [V2G20-2309] The XML schema with the namespace "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:DC" shall be used for encoding and decoding EXI streams sent or received with Part20DCMainstreamPayloadID and defined in 8.3.4.5.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the correct XML schema namespace is used for encoding and decoding EXI streams.
This atom specifies that the XML schema defined in 8.3.4.5 shall be used for encoding and decoding EXI streams associated with Part20DCMainstreamPayloadID.

V2G20-2310.text: [V2G20-2310] An element/attribute which is not defined in Annex A shall be encoded and decoded as schema deviation case according to W3C EXI 1.0.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that any element or attribute not listed in Annex A is identified.

V2G20-2450.text: [V2G20-2450] Each of the OCSP responses received by the SECC should be signed by a certificate derived from one of the root certificates supported by the SECC.
