atoms.expr: FORALL OCSPResponse IN Received_OCSPResponses: OCSPResponse.Signature.Certificate.Issuer IN SECC_SupportedRootCertificates
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that throughout the session, all received OCSP responses are signed by a certificate derived from one of the SECC's supported root certificates.

V2G20-2451.text: [V2G20-2451] Per IETF RFC 6960 (as updated by IETF RFC 8954), the SECC will verify the OCSP responder certificate before accepting the OCSP response.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the SECC verifies the OCSP responder certificate according to IETF RFC 6960 and its updates.
The SECC must perform the action of verifying the OCSP responder certificate.
This invariant ensures that the OCSP responder certificate verification has passed before the SECC accepts the OCSP response.

V2G20-2452.text: [V2G20-2452] Per IETF RFC 6960 (as updated by IETF RFC 8954), the SECC will verify the signature on the received OCSP response.

atoms.notes: This action only applies when the SECC has received an OCSP response.

V2G20-2453.text: [V2G20-2453] The validity period of the CRL provided for a vehicle certificate shall not be longer than 1 week.

atoms.notes: This constraint ensures that the CRL validity period does not exceed 1 week.

V2G20-2454.text: [V2G20-2454] In the case where the CRL for a certificate was not signed by the issuing CA of the certificate (V2G root CA, OEM root CA, OEM sub-CA1, OEM sub-CA1, OEM sub-CA2 or any corresponding cross-certified CA), each CRL shall contain the associated CRL issuer's certificate chain up to, but not including, the corresponding root.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the CRL issuer is different from the certificate issuer.
This action ensures that the CRL issuer's certificate chain is included.
This field constraint ensures the certificate chain includes all necessary certificates up to, but not including, the root CA.
This invariant ensures that all CRLs have a valid certificate chain.

atoms.expr: exists(CA in CAs, CA.type in {V2GRootCA, OEMRootCA, OEMSubCA1, OEMSubCA2, CrossCertifiedCA})
atoms.notes: This assumption states that there exist CAs of specified types.

V2G20-2455.text: [V2G20-2455] Each of the CRL received by the SECC should be signed by a certificate derived from one of the root certificates supported by the SECC.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the CRL's signature is derived from a root certificate supported by the SECC.
Ensures that the certificate used to sign the CRL is derived from a root certificate.
Assumes that the SECC has at least one supported root certificate.

V2G20-2456.text: [V2G20-2456] Per IETF RFC 5280 (as updated by IETF RFC 6818, IETF RFC 8398 and IETF RFC 8399), the SECC will verify the CRL issuer certificate before accepting the CRL.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the SECC verifies the CRL issuer certificate according to the specified IETF RFCs.
This action specifies that the SECC must perform the verification of the CRL issuer certificate.
This invariant ensures that the CRL issuer certificate verification has passed before any further actions involving the CRL are taken.
This assumption states that the CRL issuer certificate complies with the relevant IETF RFCs.

V2G20-2457.text: [V2G20-2457] Per IETF RFC 5280 (as updated by IETF RFC 6818, IETF RFC 8398 and IETF RFC 8399), the SECC will verify the signature on the received CRL.

atoms.notes: The SECC must perform a signature verification on the received Certificate Revocation List (CRL) according to the specified IETF RFCs.
The CRL must have been received before the SECC can verify its signature.
It is assumed that the SECC complies with the relevant IETF RFCs for certificate handling and verification.

V2G20-2458.text: [V2G20-2458] The SECC shall support all cipher suites defined in Table 6.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the SECC supports all cipher suites listed in Table 6.

V2G20-2459.text: [V2G20-2459] The EVCC shall support all cipher suites defined in Table 6.

V2G20-2460.text: [V2G20-2460] When selecting the named group from the list of named groups received in the "supported_groups" extension field of the received "ClientHello" message, the SECC shall give preference to the most preferred named group that the SECC supports.

atoms.notes: Ensures that the ClientHello message contains the supported_groups extension field.
The SECC selects the most preferred named group from the list of supported groups that it also supports.
Ensures that the selected named group is within the list of groups supported by the SECC.
Ensures that the selected named group is always the most preferred among those supported by both the client and the SECC.

V2G20-2461.text: [V2G20-2461] The signature algorithm selected by the SECC shall be compatible with the selected named group.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the signature algorithm chosen by the SECC is compatible with the elliptic curve named group used for key exchange.
The SECC must select a signature algorithm that is compatible with the named group specified during the key exchange process.

atoms.expr: SignatureAlgorithm remains compatible with NamedGroup throughout session
atoms.notes: Once a compatible signature algorithm and named group are selected, they should remain consistent throughout the session to ensure cryptographic integrity.

V2G20-2462.text: [V2G20-2462] The SECC shall follow the requirements defined in 7.7.3.3 and IETF RFC 8446 to setup the TLS 1.3 session.

atoms.notes: This action refers to the SECC's responsibility to establish a TLS 1.3 session following the guidelines specified in IETF RFC 8446.
This action indicates that the SECC must adhere to the specific requirements outlined in section 7.7.3.3 of the ISO 15118-20 standard for setting up the TLS session.
It is assumed that the TLS version used in the session setup process is 1.3, as required by the standard.

V2G20-2465.text: [V2G20-2465] The EVCC shall follow the requirements defined in 7.7.3.3 and IETF RFC 8446 to setup the TLS 1.3 session.

atoms.notes: The EVCC must initiate the TLS 1.3 session setup according to the specified standards.
It is assumed that both the EVCC and SECC comply with the IETF RFC 8446 for TLS 1.3.
It is assumed that both the EVCC and SECC comply with the requirements defined in section 7.7.3.3 of ISO 15118-20.

V2G20-2468.text: [V2G20-2468] The CPM4PE, if active, shall expire on the EVCC after the TLS session has been established and PE private root CA certificate was not received in the PE certificate chain.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if CPM4PE is active.
This guard checks if the TLS session has been established.
This guard checks if the PE private root CA certificate was not received.
This action represents the expiration of CPM4PE on the EVCC.
This sequence constraint ensures that CPM4PE expires only after the TLS session is established and the PE private root CA certificate is not received.

V2G20-2469.text: [V2G20-2469] The CPM4PE, if active, shall expire on the private SECC after the TLS session has been established and OEM root CA certificate was not received in the vehicle certificate chain.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the CPM4PE is active, the TLS session has been established, and the OEM root CA certificate was not received in the vehicle certificate chain.
This action specifies that the CPM4PE should be expired on the private SECC under the given conditions.
This invariant ensures that if the conditions for expiring CPM4PE are met, then CPM4PE is indeed expired.

V2G20-2470.text: [V2G20-2470] If the SECC does not support TLS session resumption, the EVCC shall setup a distinct TLS session for each value added service supported/provided by the SECC.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the SECC does not support TLS session resumption.
The EVCC shall setup a distinct TLS session for each value added service provided by the SECC.
This ensures that for each value-added service provided by the SECC, the EVCC sets up a distinct TLS session.

V2G20-2473.text: [V2G20-2473] Each message, that needs the XML signature framework shall use the value "http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#ecdsa-sha512" as algorithm attribute within the SignatureMethod element, if the algorithm defined in [V2G20-2674] shall be used according to the configuration in [V2G20-2320].

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the specified algorithm is used for messages requiring XML signatures.
This guard checks if the algorithm defined in V2G20-2674 should be used according to the configuration in V2G20-2320.

V2G20-2474.text: [V2G20-2474] Each message, that needs the XML signature framework shall use the value "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:Security:xmldsig#Ed448" as Algorithm attribute within the SignatureMethod element, if the algorithm defined in [V2G20-2319] shall be used according to the configuration in [V2G20-2320].

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the correct algorithm is used for XML signatures when specified by the configuration.
This guard checks if the algorithm defined in [V2G20-2319] is correctly configured as per [V2G20-2320].

atoms.expr: XML signature framework is required for certain messages
atoms.notes: This assumption states that some messages require the use of the XML signature framework.

V2G20-2475.text: [V2G20-2475] Each message, that needs the XML signature framework shall use the value "http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha512" as algorithm attribute within the DigestMethod element, if the algorithm defined in [V2G20-2674] shall be used according to the configuration in [V2G20-2320].

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the specified algorithm is used for messages requiring XML signature.
This guard checks if the conditions defined in V2G20-2674 and V2G20-2320 are met before applying the algorithm constraint.

V2G20-2476.text: [V2G20-2476] Each message, that needs the XML signature framework shall use the value "urn:iso:std:iso:15118:-20:Security:xmlenc#SHAKE256" as algorithm attribute within the DigestMethod element, if the algorithm defined in [V2G20-2318] shall be used according to the configuration in [V2G20-2320].

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the specified algorithm is used for messages requiring XML signature, as per the configuration.
This guard checks if the algorithm defined in V2G20-2318 should be used according to the configuration in V2G20-2320.

V2G20-2477.text: [V2G20-2477] Each V2G entity generating XML signatures shall utilize the private key associated with the "subjectKeyInfo" parameter of the appropriate certificate, as specified in Table 17, to generate the XML signatures.

atoms.notes: This action specifies that both the EVCC and SECC must use the private key from the 'subjectKeyInfo' parameter of their respective certificates to generate XML signatures.
This guard ensures that the certificate used by each V2G entity contains the 'subjectKeyInfo' parameter as specified in Table 17.
This assumption states that the certificate used by each V2G entity is valid and can be trusted.

V2G20-2478.text: [V2G20-2478] Each V2G entity verifying XML signatures shall utilize the public key included in the "subjectPublicKeyInfo" parameter of the appropriate certificate, as specified in Table 17, to verify the XML signatures.

atoms.notes: This action specifies that both EVCC and SECC must use the public key from the certificate's subjectPublicKeyInfo to verify XML signatures.
This guard ensures that the subjectPublicKeyInfo is present in the certificate before attempting to verify the signature.
This assumption states that the certificate used for extracting the public key is valid and trusted by the V2G entity.

V2G20-2479.text: [V2G20-2479] The SA receiving a CertificateInstallationReq indicating the SignatureMethod as defined by [V2G20-2474] shall use the public key in "subjectPublicKeyInfo" of the OEM provisioning certificate contained in CertificateInstallationReq message to verify the signature.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the SignatureMethod in the CertificateInstallationReq matches the definition provided by [V2G20-2474].
The SECC uses the public key from the subjectPublicKeyInfo field of the OEM provisioning certificate within the CertificateInstallationReq message to verify the signature.
Ensures that the CertificateInstallationReq message includes the subjectPublicKeyInfo field which holds the public key used for signature verification.

atoms.expr: CertificateInstallationReq contains valid OEM provisioning certificate
atoms.notes: Assumes that the CertificateInstallationReq message sent by the EVCC contains a valid OEM provisioning certificate.

V2G20-2480.text: [V2G20-2480] Unless specified otherwise, the SA (eMSP) shall use big-endian order for all bit strings and calculations specified by this subclause and the subclauses within.

V2G20-2481.text: [V2G20-2481] Unless specified otherwise, the EVCC shall use big-endian order for all bit strings and calculations specified by this subclause and the subclauses within.

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the EVCC consistently uses big-endian byte order for all bit strings and calculations as required by the standard.

V2G20-2488.text: [V2G20-2488] If the SA uses the elliptic curve corresponding to signature algorithm specified by [V2G20-2319] for contract certificate private key encryption key generation via ECDHE as specified in 7.9.2.5.4, it shall set ECDHCurve parameter in SignedInstallationDataType element of CertificateInstallationRes message to "X448".

V2G20-2489.text: [V2G20-2489] The ephemeral public key used in requirement [V2G20-2497] shall be contained in the XML element "DHPublicKey" encoded in its uncompressed form as "Subject Public Key" as defined in IETF RFC 5480.

atoms.expr: DHPublicKey is present and contains the uncompressed form of the ephemeral public key
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the DHPublicKey field is correctly populated with the uncompressed form of the ephemeral public key as required by IETF RFC 5480.

atoms.expr: DHPublicKey is encoded as 'Subject Public Key' according to IETF RFC 5480
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the encoding of the DHPublicKey follows the specifications outlined in IETF RFC 5480 for 'Subject Public Key'.
This guard ensures that the requirement [V2G20-2497] has been satisfied before proceeding with the inclusion of the ephemeral public key in the DHPublicKey field.

V2G20-2491.text: [V2G20-2491] Each V2G entity shall have mechanisms to process ECDHE Key exchange.

atoms.notes: This atom represents the requirement for both EVCC and SECC to implement the processing mechanism for ECDHE Key Exchange.

V2G20-2492.text: [V2G20-2492] Additional authenticated data (AAD) shall be calculated by concatenating the PCID received/used in the CertificateInstallationReq message with capital letters and digits without separators (18 bytes), followed by the SKI value of the contract certificate included in the CertificateInstallationRes encoded as a hexa-decimal string with capital letters and digits according to IETF RFC 5234 (16 bytes).

atoms.notes: The AAD calculation involves specific formatting rules for PCID and SKI.
The PCID part of AAD must be exactly 18 bytes long after formatting.
The SKI part of AAD must be exactly 16 bytes long when encoded as a hexadecimal string.
The PCID must be formatted with only uppercase letters and digits, no separators.
The SKI must be formatted as a hexadecimal string with only uppercase letters and digits.

V2G20-2493.text: [V2G20-2493] The private key corresponding to the contract certificate shall be transmitted only in encrypted format within SECP521_EncryptedPrivateKey or X448_EncryptedPrivateKey element in the SignedInstallationData parameter of the CertificateInstallationRes message.

atoms.notes: Ensures that the private key is transmitted in encrypted format.
Ensures that either SECP521_EncryptedPrivateKey or X448_EncryptedPrivateKey is mandatory.
Ensures that the fields belong to their respective domains.
Ensures that only one of the encrypted private key elements is present at any time.

V2G20-2494.text: [V2G20-2494] The sender shall ensure that the authenticated encryption function used to encrypt data produces an authentication tag (also known as "tag" for short) of 128 bits.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that any message requiring authenticated encryption uses a 128-bit authentication tag.

V2G20-2495.text: [V2G20-2495] When using 448-bit ephemeral public key in requirement [V2G20-2497], the sender shall not include any extra filler/padding bytes to reach DHPublicKey size of 133 bytes.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the DHPublicKey size is exactly 133 bytes when using a 448-bit ephemeral public key.
The sender shall not include any extra filler/padding bytes to reach the specified DHPublicKey size.
This constraint specifies that the DHPublicKey type should be 448-bit when the requirement applies.

atoms.expr: DHPublicKeySize == 133 AND NOT IncludeExtraPaddingBytes WHEN DHPublicKey.type == '448-bit'
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that when a 448-bit ephemeral public key is used, the DHPublicKey size is 133 bytes without any extra padding.

V2G20-2496.text: [V2G20-2496] Once the sender sends the data to the certificate provisioning service (CPS) for verification and signature generation, the sender shall irretrievably erase/delete/destroy the contract certificate private key, ECDHE private key and the session key as generated in 7.9.2.5.4, and the ciphertext.

atoms.notes: The contract certificate private key must be erased after sending data to CPS.
The ECDHE private key must be erased after sending data to CPS.
The session key must be erased after sending data to CPS.
The ciphertext must be erased after sending data to CPS.
This action only applies once the data has been sent to the CPS.

V2G20-2497.text: [V2G20-2489] The ephemeral public key used in requirement [V2G20-2497] shall be contained in the XML element "DHPublicKey" encoded in its uncompressed form as "Subject Public Key" as defined in IETF RFC 5480.

atoms.expr: DHPublicKey is present and contains SubjectPublicKey in uncompressed form as per IETF RFC 5480
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the DHPublicKey field contains the SubjectPublicKey in the correct format as specified by IETF RFC 5480.

atoms.expr: The ephemeral public key used in requirement [V2G20-2497] is always encoded according to IETF RFC 5480
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that any ephemeral public key used in the context of requirement [V2G20-2497] adheres to the encoding rules specified in IETF RFC 5480.
The AC_ChargeLoopReq must be sent within the specified timeout.
Ensures the SessionID field is correctly populated.
Ensures the PowerDeliveryReq field contains a valid parameter.

V2G20-2500.text: The byte order of all input data elements for AES-GCM-256 encryption, as specified by [V2G20-2500], shall be big-endian.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that all input data elements used for AES-GCM-256 encryption follow the big-endian byte order.

V2G20-2503.text: [V2G20-2503] The receiver shall ensure that the authenticated decryption function used to decrypt data can take an authentication tag (also known as "tag" for short) of 128 bits as the second input.

atoms.notes: This atom ensures that the AuthenticationTag used in the authenticated decryption function is 128 bits long.
This atom specifies that the receiver must use an authenticated decryption function with the AuthenticationTag as the second input.

V2G20-2504.text: [V2G20-2504] If the decryption of either the 521-bit private key or 448-bit private key or both fails, the receiver shall reject the CertificateInstallationRes message as invalid.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the decryption of either the 521-bit or 448-bit private key has failed.
This action specifies that the receiver should reject the CertificateInstallationRes message if the decryption check fails.
This invariant ensures that whenever the decryption of either private key fails, the CertificateInstallationRes message is rejected.

V2G20-2506.text: [V2G20-2506] The EVCC shall use the 521 least significant bits of the decrypted data as the 521 bit contract certificate private key.

atoms.expr: EVCC shall use the 521 least significant bits of DecryptedData as ContractCertificatePrivateKey
atoms.notes: This action specifies how the EVCC processes the decrypted data to derive the contract certificate private key.
Ensures that the derived ContractCertificatePrivateKey has exactly 521 bits.
Ensures that the ContractCertificatePrivateKey is correctly extracted from the least significant bits of DecryptedData.

V2G20-2508.text: [V2G20-2508] Upon reception of X448_EncryptedPrivateKey, the receiver (EVCC) shall decrypt the contract certificate private key using the same session key used to decrypt the 521-bit private key in [V2G20-2505] and applying the algorithm AES-GCM-256 according to NIST Special Publication 800-38D.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the EVCC has received the X448_EncryptedPrivateKey message.
The EVCC shall decrypt the contract certificate private key using the specified session key and AES-GCM-256 algorithm.
The session key used for decryption must be the same as the one used in V2G20-2505.
Assumes that the AES-GCM-256 algorithm is correctly implemented according to NIST Special Publication 800-38D.

V2G20-2509.text: [V2G20-2509] The EVCC shall use the 448 bit decrypted data as the 448 bit contract certificate private key.

atoms.notes: This action specifies that the EVCC should assign the decrypted data to the contract certificate private key.
Ensures that the decrypted data used for the contract certificate private key is exactly 448 bits long.
Ensures that the contract certificate private key is exactly 448 bits long after assignment.

V2G20-2510.text: [V2G20-2510] Upon receipt of a contract certificate, the EVCC shall verify that the 448 bit private key received with the certificate is a valid 448 bit private key for that certificate:

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the EVCC has received a contract certificate.
The EVCC shall perform the action of verifying the private key against the received certificate.
Ensures that the length of the private key is exactly 448 bits.
This invariant ensures that the private key is valid for the given certificate throughout the session.

V2G20-2511.text: [V2G20-2511] The EVCC's TPM 2.0 shall contain a storage key pair.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the EVCC's TPM 2.0 contains a storage key pair, which is a global requirement for the EVCC.

V2G20-2512.text: [V2G20-2512] The OEM provisioning key pair shall be generated using the provisioning key profile from Table 19 for the default ECC algorithm (see [V2G20-2674]) or a separately defined TPM key profile for an alternative ECC algorithm (see [V2G20-2319]).

atoms.notes: The action specifies that the EVCC should generate a key pair based on the provisioning key profile.
This constraint ensures that the provisioning key profile used is either the default ECC algorithm profile or an alternative TPM key profile.
Assumes that the default ECC algorithm profile is correctly defined and available in Table 19.
Assumes that an alternative TPM key profile is defined separately if not using the default ECC algorithm.

V2G20-2513.text: [V2G20-2513] If the OEM provisioning key pair is generated outside the TPM, the parameters "fixedTPM" and "fixedParent" in the "objectAttributes" field of the public area shall be set to 0.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the OEM provisioning key pair is generated outside the TPM.
This action sets the 'fixedTPM' and 'fixedParent' parameters to 0 when the OEM provisioning key pair is generated outside the TPM.

V2G20-2514.text: [V2G20-2514] The OEM provisioning key pair shall be stored in the EVCC's TPM underneath the storage key corresponding to the ECC algorithm used to generate this key (see [V2G20-2320]).

atoms.notes: This action specifies where the OEM provisioning key pair should be stored within the EVCC's TPM.
This guard ensures that there exists a storage key in the TPM corresponding to the ECC algorithm used for generating the OEM provisioning key pair.
This assumption ensures that the ECC algorithm used to generate the OEM provisioning key pair matches the expected algorithm.

V2G20-2515.text: [V2G20-2515] If the OEM provisioning key pair in the EVCC's TPM is desired to be sealed to an OEM specific policy, this policy shall be provided in the "authPolicy" of the key (see Table 19).

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the OEM provisioning key pair in the EVCC's TPM is desired to be sealed.
This action sets the 'authPolicy' of the key to an OEM-specific policy when sealing is desired.
This field constraint ensures that the type of 'authPolicy' is set to an OEM-specific policy type.
This invariant ensures that whenever the OEM provisioning key pair is sealed, the 'authPolicy' is set to the OEM-specific policy.

V2G20-2516.text: [V2G20-2516] The OEM provisioning certificate for an OEM provisioning public key shall include the public key of its parent storage key pair in the EVCC's TPM to be used in ECDHE into the "TPMStorageKey" extension of the OEM provisioning certificate as defined in [V2G20-2594] and [V2G20-1226].

atoms.notes: This atom checks that the TPMStorageKey extension is present in the OEM provisioning certificate.
This atom ensures that throughout the session, the TPMStorageKey extension in the OEM provisioning certificate consistently contains the correct parent storage public key.

atoms.expr: ParentStoragePublicKey is stored in EVCC's TPM
atoms.notes: This atom assumes that the parent storage public key is correctly stored in the EVCC's TPM.

V2G20-2517.text: [V2G20-2517] If the contract certificate keys are supposed to be sealed to a policy, the digest of the EVCC's TPM policy shall be included in the "TPMPPolicyDigest" extension of the OEM provisioning certificate as defined in [V2G20-2594] and [V2G20-1226].

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the contract certificate keys are supposed to be sealed to a policy.
This action specifies that the digest of the EVCC's TPM policy shall be included in the 'TPMPPolicyDigest' extension of the OEM provisioning certificate.
This field constraint ensures that the TPMPPolicyDigest field is of type 'digest' and is mandatory in the OEM provisioning certificate.
This assumption relies on the definitions provided in requirements V2G20-2594 and V2G20-1226 for the TPM policy digest.

V2G20-2518.text: [V2G20-2518] In order to enable a direct import of the encrypted contract certificate private key into the EVCC's TPM, the contract certificate private key shall be encrypted with the TPM storage key of the EVCC's TPM from the OEM provisioning certificate extension (in contrast to [V2G20-2529] and [V2G20-2530]).

atoms.notes: The EVCC must have a valid TPM storage key for the encryption process.
The encrypted contract certificate private key must not be null after encryption.

V2G20-2519.text: [V2G20-2519] The encryption, as specified by [V2G20-2518], requires the generation of a new seed (session key).

atoms.notes: This action is derived from the requirement to generate a new seed for encryption as per [V2G20-2518].
This guard ensures that encryption is required before generating a new seed.
This invariant ensures that each session uses a unique session key.

V2G20-2520.text: [V2G20-2520] The ephemeral public key of the eMSP (SA) shall be transmitted using the method defined in [V2G20-2489].

atoms.notes: The action of transmitting the ephemeral public key is derived from the requirement text.
The field EphemeralPublicKey must be transmitted according to the method defined in another requirement.
It is assumed that the method for transmitting the ephemeral public key as defined in [V2G20-2489] exists and is correctly implemented.

V2G20-2521.text: [V2G20-2521] The encrypted contract certificate private key shall be transmitted within TPM_EncryptedPrivateKey in the message CertificateInstallationRes if the private contract key was encrypted with the public storage key from the OEM provisioning certificate extension carrying TPM Information.

atoms.notes: Checks if the private contract key was encrypted with the public storage key from the OEM provisioning certificate extension carrying TPM Information.
Transmits the encrypted contract certificate private key within TPM_EncryptedPrivateKey in the CertificateInstallationRes message.
Ensures that TPM_EncryptedPrivateKey is a mandatory field when the condition is met.
The SECC must respond within the specified timeout period.
The SECC should send AC_ChargeLoopRes following receipt of AC_ChargeLoopReq.
The SessionID must not change during the session.

atoms.expr: EVCC correctly formats messages according to ISO 15118-20
atoms.notes: It is assumed that the EVCC sends well-formed messages.
EVCC sends PaymentServiceSelectionReq after receiving the correct response.
The PaymentServiceSelectionReq must be sent within the defined timeout.
Ensures the PaymentServiceSelection field is mandatory in the request.
Defines the sequence where PaymentServiceSelectionReq follows SVCSPaymentServiceSelectionRes.

V2G20-2524.text: [V2G20-2524] The SA (eMSP) shall support calculation of the ECDHE secret and the key derivation function, as specified by NIST Special Publication 800-56A, for the encryption of private keys.

V2G20-2525.text: [V2G20-2525] The EVCC shall support calculation of the ECDHE secret and the key derivation function, as specified by NIST Special Publication 800-56A, for the decryption of encrypted information like private keys.

atoms.expr: EVCC supports ECDHE_secret_calculation AND EVCC supports key_derivation_function
atoms.notes: This action ensures the EVCC has the capability to perform cryptographic operations necessary for secure communication.
This invariant ensures that the cryptographic functions used by the EVCC comply with the specified standard.
This assumption relies on the validity and correctness of the referenced NIST publication.

V2G20-2526.text: [V2G20-2526] When the mechanism defined by [V2G20-2320] indicates usage of the (elliptic curve) EC as specified by [V2G20-2674], the SA (eMSP) shall generate a 521 bit ephemeral public/private key pair using elliptic curve secp521r1[SECG notation] as specified by NIST Special Publication 800-56A.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the mechanism defined by V2G20-2320 indicates the usage of elliptic curve cryptography.
This guard ensures that the elliptic curve specification used is as defined by V2G20-2674.

V2G20-2527.text: [V2G20-2527] When the mechanism defined by [V2G20-2320] indicates usage of the curve corresponding to the signature algorithm specified by [V2G20-2319], the SA (eMSP) shall generate a 448 bit ephemeral public/private key pair using ECC algorithm X448 as specified by IETF RFC 7748.

V2G20-2529.text: [V2G20-2518] In order to enable a direct import of the encrypted contract certificate private key into the EVCC's TPM, the contract certificate private key shall be encrypted with the TPM storage key of the EVCC's TPM from the OEM provisioning certificate extension (in contrast to [V2G20-2529] and [V2G20-2530]).

Ensure that the OEM provisioning certificate extension is present before attempting to encrypt the private key.

V2G20-2530.text: [V2G20-2518] In order to enable a direct import of the encrypted contract certificate private key into the EVCC's TPM, the contract certificate private key shall be encrypted with the TPM storage key of the EVCC's TPM from the OEM provisioning certificate extension (in contrast to [V2G20-2529] and [V2G20-2530]).

atoms.notes: The OEM provisioning certificate extension must exist for the encryption process.
It is assumed that the EVCC's TPM storage key is valid and available for encryption.

V2G20-2531.text: [V2G20-2531] When the EVCC receives the parameter ECDHCurve set to "SECP521", it shall use the 1056 least significant bits of the DHPublicKey as the public key in calculation of the session key as defined by [V2G20-2535].

atoms.notes: Ensures that ECDHCurve is properly defined and can take the value 'SECP521'.

V2G20-2532.text: [V2G20-2532] When the EVCC receives the parameter ECDHCurve set to "X448", it shall use the 448 least significant bits of the DHPublicKey as the public key in calculation of the session key as defined by [V2G20-2535].

atoms.notes: This action specifies that the EVCC should use the OEM provisioning certificate private key and the public key calculated according to [V2G20-2531] for calculating the session key.

atoms.expr: [V2G20-2531] has been correctly executed and the public key is available
atoms.notes: This assumption relies on the correct execution of [V2G20-2531] to ensure the availability of the public key needed for session key calculation.

V2G20-2534.text: [V2G20-2534] If the EVCC receives the parameter ECDHCurve set to "X448", it shall use the private key associated with the "Alternate Subject Public Key" of the OEM provisioning certificate along with the public key calculated from [V2G20-2532] for calculation of the session key as defined by [V2G20-2535].

V2G20-2535.text: The seed shall be generated using the method defined in 7.9.2.5.3., with the "TPM storage key" from the OEM provisioning certificate extension used as static public key for calculation of the session key as defined by [V2G20-2535].

atoms.notes: The seed generation process uses the TPM storage key from the OEM provisioning certificate.
Ensures the correct static public key is used for the session key calculation.
The seed must be of type 'generated_seed' as per the specified method.
The session key must be calculated correctly based on the generated seed and the TPM storage key.

V2G20-2539.text: [V2G20-2539] If the EVCC received SessionSetupRes message with the ResponseCode set to "OK_OldSessionJoined" and the SessionID set to the same value that it sent in SessionSetupReq message to resume the previously paused V2G communication session, the EVCC shall check that it is still connected to the same SECC with which it had initially setup this particular V2G communication session.

atoms.notes: Checks if the received ResponseCode is OK_OldSessionJoined and the SessionID matches the one sent in SessionSetupReq.
The EVCC shall verify that it is still connected to the same SECC as before.

V2G20-2541.text: [V2G20-2541] If the EVCC detects that there has been no communication associated with a particular V2G session for 648 000 s (7,5 days), the EVCC shall immediately terminate/close that V2G session.

atoms.notes: This atom represents the timeout condition where the EVCC monitors the duration since the last communication.
This atom specifies the action the EVCC must take when the timeout condition is met.

V2G20-2546.text: [V2G20-2546] If the V2G communication session is resumed according to [V2G20-2545] and if the SECC wants to change the energy transfer parameters listed in [V2G20-1058], it shall use the schedule renegotiation mechanism defined in this document.

Assumes that the energy transfer parameters listed in [V2G20-1058] are valid and applicable for renegotiation.

atoms.notes: This guard checks if a new SessionID was assigned according to either V2G20-2627 or V2G20-2547.
The SECC shall consider the current interaction as a new V2G session when the guard condition is met.
This invariant ensures that whenever a new SessionID is detected, the current session is treated as a new one.

V2G20-2550.text: [V2G20-2631] The SECC should securely store the hash generated by [V2G20-2630] until it is used per [V2G20-2550].

atoms.notes: The SECC must perform the action of storing the hash.
The hash must be non-null before it can be stored.
Once stored, the SECC's stored hash must match the original hash.
After the hash is used, the SECC must clear the stored hash.
It is assumed that the storage mechanism used by the SECC is secure.

V2G20-2551.text: [V2G20-2551] The SECC shall discard the hash generated by [V2G20-2630] after the hash has been utilized per [V2G20-2550].

atoms.notes: The SECC discards the hash after its utilization.
The SECC discards the hash only after it has been utilized.
The hash must have been utilized before discarding.

atoms.notes: Ensures the correct session is being referenced.
The SECC stores the hash value securely.
The hash remains stored until the session ends.
The stored hash is deleted when the session is terminated.

V2G20-2553.text: [V2G20-2632] The SECC should securely store the hash generated by [V2G20-2553] until it is used per [V2G20-2633].

atoms.notes: The hash must be stored until it is used according to V2G20-2633.

V2G20-2554.text: [V2G20-2554] The SECC should check that the hash value calculated by [V2G20-2633] is the same as the hash value calculated by [V2G20-2550].

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the hash value calculated by the SECC matches the hash value calculated by the EVCC as per requirements V2G20-2633 and V2G20-2550.

atoms.notes: Assumes that the EVCC has correctly calculated the hash value as specified in requirement V2G20-2550.

atoms.expr: hashValue_SECC is correctly calculated according to V2G20-2633
atoms.notes: Assumes that the SECC has correctly calculated the hash value as specified in requirement V2G20-2633.

V2G20-2555.text: [V2G20-2636] The EVCC should securely store the hash generated by [V2G20-2635] until it is used per [V2G20-2555].

atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that the hash generated by the process described in [V2G20-2635] is securely stored by the EVCC until it is utilized according to the requirements specified in [V2G20-2555].

V2G20-2556.text: [V2G20-2556] The EVCC should discard the hash generated by [V2G20-2635] after the hash has been utilized per [V2G20-2555].

atoms.notes: This action specifies that the EVCC should discard the hash once it has been used according to the rules defined in V2G20-2555.
This guard ensures that the hash generated by V2G20-2635 can only be discarded if it has already been utilized as specified in V2G20-2555.

V2G20-2557.text: [V2G20-2557] The EVCC should securely store the hash generated by [V2G20-2555] until the V2G session associated with the particular SessionID is terminated/closed.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the session is not yet terminated or closed.
The EVCC should store the hash generated by the process described in V2G20-2555.
The stored hash must remain unchanged and equal to the hash generated by V2G20-2555 throughout the session.
When the session is terminated or closed, the stored hash should be cleared.

V2G20-2558.text: [V2G20-2558] Whenever the EVCC performs the "Full Handshake" (as described in 7.7.3.5) to setup a TLS session (as described in 7.7.3.3, 7.7.3.4 and 7.7.3.5), it shall calculate a new session binding by following [V2G20-2635].

atoms.notes: This guard checks if the EVCC is performing the 'Full Handshake' process.
The EVCC shall calculate a new session binding according to [V2G20-2635].
The calculation of the new session binding should occur after the completion of the Full Handshake.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that the hash value calculated by the EVCC according to V2G20-2638 matches the hash value calculated by the SECC according to V2G20-2555.

V2G20-2563.text: [V2G20-2563] In case of EIM, the SECC shall complete the authorization at the SECC and provide appropriate response to the EVCC via AuthorizationRes.

V2G20-2567.text: [V2G20-2567] If the SECC offers only EIM as an authorization service, it shall include parameter EIM_ASResAuthorizationMode in AuthorizationSetupRes message.

V2G20-2571.text: [V2G20-2571] The EVCC shall stop sending CertificateInstallationReq if the maximum number of contract certificates that can be installed, as indicated by the parameter MaximumContractCertificateChains in CertificateInstallationReq, has been reached while the parameter RemainingContractCertificateChains of the CertificateInstallationRes is greater than zero.

V2G20-2686.text: [V2G20-2686] The relying party shall reject any certificate that contains an extension or field/parameter/attribute/data type not defined in the certificate profile for that certificate type in this document.

atoms.notes: This guard ensures that any certificate received by either the EVCC or SECC does not contain undefined extensions, fields, parameters, attributes, or data types according to the specified certificate profile.

atoms.expr: ALL certificates MUST conform TO defined_extensions, defined_fields, defined_parameters, defined_attributes, AND defined_data_types
atoms.notes: This invariant ensures that all certificates processed within the session must adhere to the defined certificate profile.

V2G20-2687.text: [V2G20-2687] All mandatory/required fields/parameters/attributes/data types shall be included in a certificate conforming to a particular certificate profile.

atoms.expr: forall field in CertificateProfile : if field.isMandatory then field.isPresent
atoms.notes: This atom ensures that all fields marked as mandatory within a given certificate profile are indeed present in the certificate.

V2G20-2688.text: [V2G20-2688] Any optional fields/parameters/attributes/data types may or may not be included in the certificate at the CA's discretion, unless specified otherwise by the requirements in this document.

atoms.notes: This atom captures the general rule that optional fields in certificates can be included or omitted at the CA's discretion.
This atom captures the exception to the general rule, where specific requirements in the document may override the CA's discretion.

V2G20-2693.text: [V2G20-2693] If the optional field/parameter/attribute/data type is included in a certificate, then any sub-fields/sub-parameters/sub-attributes/sub-data types (within the optional field/parameter/attribute/data type) marked as optional in the certificate profile may or may not be included, at the CA's discretion (unless specified otherwise by the requirements in this document), in the certificate conforming to the particular certificate profile.

atoms.expr: if OptionalFieldIncludedInCertificate == true then SubFieldsMarkedOptionalInProfile MAY be included
atoms.notes: This atom captures the condition where if an optional field is included in a certificate, its sub-fields marked as optional can be included at the CA's discretion.

atoms.notes: This atom represents the assumption that unless explicitly stated otherwise, the CA has the discretion to include or exclude sub-fields marked as optional.

V2G20-2695.text: [V2G20-2695] The relying party shall reject a certificate that does not contain either "Version", "SerialNumber", "Signature", "Issuer", "Validity", "Subject" or "SubjectPublicKeyInfo" in "TbsCertificate" field.

atoms.expr: !(TbsCertificate.Version && TbsCertificate.SerialNumber && TbsCertificate.Signature && TbsCertificate.Issuer && TbsCertificate.Validity && TbsCertificate.Subject && TbsCertificate.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)

V2G20-2699.text: [V2G20-2699] When generating or verifying the XML signatures, each V2G entity shall utilize the public/private key associated with the appropriate certificate (as specified in Table 17) that uses the algorithm as indicated by the configuration in [V2G20-2320].

V2G20-2707.text: [V2G20-2707] Upon reception of SignedInstallationData, the EVCC shall check that the received encrypted contract key uses the ECC algorithm in accordance with the configuration parameter [V2G20-2320] or with the OEM provisioning certificate the EVCC provided in the CertificateInstallationReq, otherwise, the EVCC shall regard the received message as invalid, and discard the message.

V2G20-4013.text: [V2G20-4013] In case of an EV error the EVCC shall send a ACDP_SystemStatusReq message with Parameter "EV_Status_ReadyToCharge = FALSE" and all EV parameters representing the current EV (error) status and the EVCC shall execute normal shut down of the charging process according to Figure 92.
